06.4Chapter 6 — Reinforcement Learning

6.1.5–6.1.8 GRPO, GSPO, CISPO aur comparison

PPO ke baad reasoning era ne naye algorithms diye — GRPO, GSPO aur CISPO — jo value function hatane, sequence-level ratios aur token dropping fix karne par focus karte hain.

GRPO — value function ke bina PPO

Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) DeepSeekMath me introduce hua aur DeepSeek-V3 aur DeepSeek-R1 jaise works me use hua. GRPO ko PPO-inspired algorithm ke roop me dekha jaa sakta hai, bahut similar surrogate loss ke saath — lekin ye value function seekhna avoid karta hai, original policy language model ki ek aur copy se. Iske do posited benefits: (1) LM backbone se value function seekhne ki challenge avoid karna, jahan best practices establish nahi hui hain; (2) memory bachana — extra model weights memory me rakhne ki zaroorat nahi (current policy + reference policy + value function ki jagah sirf pehle do copies).

GRPO value estimation simplify karta hai: episode (prompt ka completion) ke har token ko wahi value assign karta hai — discounted rewards ke bajay — advantage ya baseline estimate karke. Estimate same initial state/prompt se multiple completions aur rewards collect karke kiya jaata hai (Monte Carlo estimate).

Equation 6.26 (GRPO objective): J(θ) = (1/G) × Σi=1..G ( min( (πθ(ai|s)/πθold(ai|s)) × Ai, clip(πθ/πθold, 1−ε, 1+ε) × Ai ) − β × DKL(πθ∥πref) ), jahan G ek prompt ke completions ka group hai. PPO ke relative, standard GRPO implementation me KL distance loss me include hoti hai.
Equation 6.28 (GRPO advantage): Ai = (ri − mean(r1, …, rG)) / std(r1, …, rG). Intuitively, GRPO update ek hi sawaal ke multiple jawaabon ko batch ke andar compare karta hai — model correct mark kiye gaye jawaabon jaisa ban-na seekhta hai aur doosron jaisa kam.

GRPO advantage computation me trade-offs hain: standard deviation se normalize karna un questions ko reward karta hai jinke batch me answer correctness me kam variation hai. Jin questions ke lagbhag saare answers correct ya saare incorrect hote hain, unka std kam hoga aur advantage zyada hoga. Ek paper ne std term hatane ka proposal diya — lekin iski keemat ye hai ki woh questions down-weight ho jaate hain jahan saare incorrect the aur kuch correct the — jo valuable learning signal ho sakta hai. High-variance prompts exactly hardest cases ho sakte hain, jahan sirf kuch sampled completions correct answer dhoondhte hain aur strong training signal dete hain.

Dr. GRPO (GRPO Done Right) std normalization term hatata hai — isse advantage scale up hota hai, jo answer scores me variance wale samples par GRPO learning rate badhane ke equivalent hai. Dr. GRPO ka advantage: Ãi = ri − mean(r1, …, rG) (Eq 6.29). Aur ye RLOO estimation ke equivalent hai, constant scaling factor tak (jo normally matter nahi karta kyunki advantage normalize karne ki implementation details hain) — Eq 6.30/6.31 me derivation dikhaya gaya hai ki (G/(G−1)) × Ãi = AiRLOO.

GSPO — sequence-level importance ratios

PPO aur GRPO token level par importance sampling apply karte hain aur surrogate objective clip karke learning stabilize karte hain. Lekin isme ek subtle failure mode hai: jab kisi token ka importance ratio clipping range [1−ε, 1+ε] se bahar chala jaata hai, to us token ko zero gradient milta hai. Rare lekin important tokens — jaise key reasoning steps jinhe model initially low probability assign karta hai — ke liye ye "token dropping" model ko unhe reliably produce karna seekhne se rok sakta hai.

Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) GRPO ko extend karta hai: importance ratios token level ke bajay sequence level par compute karta hai. Practical motivation: per-token importance sampling ratio aksar numerically unstable hota hai. Conceptual motivation: jab rewards sequence level par assign hote hain (jaise most RLHF aur RLVR setups me), to importance sampling correction bhi usi granularity par hona chahiye.

Equation 6.34 (GSPO sequence ratio): ρi(θ) = ( πθ(ai|s) / πθold(ai|s) )1/|ai| = exp( (1/|ai|) × Σt=1..|ai| log( πθ(ai,t|s,ai,<t) / πθold(ai,t|s,ai,<t) ) ) — length-normalized geometric mean, taaki lambi sequences me numerical issues na aayein.
Equation 6.35 (GSPO objective): JGSPO(θ) = E[ (1/G) × Σi=1..G min(ρi(θ)Ai, clip(ρi(θ), 1−ε, 1+ε)Ai) ]. Advantage computation GRPO jaisi hi rehti hai (Eq 6.28). Summary: "GRPO with sequence-level importance ratios".

CISPO — weights clip karo, objective nahi

Clipped Importance Sampling Policy Optimization (CISPO) alag approach leta hai: surrogate objective clip karne ke bajay importance weights ko hi clip karta hai, saath me saare tokens ke gradients preserve karta hai. Objective clipped importance weight par stop-gradient use karta hai, PPO-style two-sided clipping ke bajay REINFORCE-style formulation me wapas jaata hai.

Equation 6.36 (CISPO objective): JCISPO(θ) = E[ (1/Σ|ai|) × Σi Σt sg(ρ̂i,t(θ)) × Ai,t × log πθ(ai,t|s,ai,<t) ], jahan sg(·) stop-gradient hai.
Equation 6.37: ρ̂i,t(θ) = clip(ρi,t(θ), 1−εlow, 1+εhigh), ρi,t(θ) = πθ/πθold.

PPO/GRPO se key difference subtle lekin important hai: weight clip karne (objective nahi) ka matlab hai har token ko ab bhi uske advantage ke proportional gradient signal milta hai — weight sirf ye bound karta hai ki importance ratio us signal ko kitna amplify ya suppress kare. Ye ek bias-variance tradeoff hai: weights clip karne se bias aata hai lekin variance control hoti hai, aur critically, token gradients poori tarah drop hone se bachte hain. CISPO asymmetric clipping bounds bhi allow karta hai (εlow ≠ εhigh) — jaise DAPO ka "clip-higher" modification — jo exploration encourage kar sakta hai, un tokens ke liye bade updates allow karke jinhe model upweight karna chahta hai.

GSPO aur CISPO dono un organizations ne develop kiye jo large-scale MoE models par RL apply karne ki limits push kar rahe the — MoE models apne numerical issues ke liye known hain. Papers highlight karte hain ki per-token importance sampling ratios unstable hote hain aur gradients me substantial variance add kar sakte hain, learning mitigate karte hue. Ye algorithms large-scale models par khaas taur par impactful ho sakte hain, lekin chhote academic experiments me kam studied aur beneficial hain. Related work: TOPR (Tapered Off-Policy REINFORCE) bhi IS weights ko seedha clip karta hai (CISPO jaisa), lekin sequence level par (GSPO jaisa) aur reward sign ke basis par asymmetric clipping use karta hai — positive rewards ke liye koi IS correction nahi, negative rewards ke liye ratios ko [0, 1] me clip karna.

Table 6.1 — algorithms ki comparison

MethodTypeReward ModelValue FunctionReference PolicyCore Loss
REINFORCEOn-policyYesNoNo−(1/T) Σ log πθ(at|st)(Gt − b(st))
RLOOOn-policyYesNoNoLeave-one-out baseline ke saath REINFORCE jaisa
CISPOOn-policyYesNoYes−Σ sg(ρ̂i,t)Ai,t log πθ
PPOOn-policyYesYesYes−(1/T) Σ min(ρtAt, clip(ρt, 1−ε, 1+ε)At)

Note: on/off-policy yahan derivation ko indicate karta hai (practice me most thode off-policy apply hote hain). Reference policy ka matlab hai ki optimization ke liye hi chahiye, KL penalty ke liye nahi.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 6

06.5Chapter 6 — Reinforcement Learning

6.2 Implementation — loss aggregation, async, PPO/GRPO code

Original Deep RL literature ke comparison me language models ke liye RL implement karne me kai chhoti implementation details hoti hain. Ye section woh key factors highlight karta hai jo popular algorithms ki implementations ko differentiate karte hain.

Pehle — EOS truncation aur misc details

RLHF me ek crucial step hai text generate karna jo phir reward model se rate hoga. Normally model ko end-of-sequence (EOS) token generate karna chahiye jo bataye ki generation khatm hui, lekin common practice hai generation length par hard cap lagana taaki infrastructure efficiently use ho. RLHF ka ek failure mode ye hai ki model ke answers regularly truncate ho jaate hain, jo reward model ki ratings ko out-of-distribution aur unpredictable bana deta hai. Solution: reward model scoring sirf eos_token par chalana, aur bahut lambi generation ke liye model ko penalty dena.

Popular open-source RLHF tools me algorithms ke across implementation details me bada variance hai. Kuch decisions jo yahan cover nahi hain: value network initialization (InstructGPT me standard: value network ko RLHF me use hone wale reward model se initialize karna; doosre SFT checkpoint + randomly initialized value head use karte hain); reward normalization / whitening (normalization rewards ko 0–1 ke beech bound karta hai; whitening zero mean aur unit variance me transform karke stability aur boost deta hai); different KL estimators (exact KL compute karna complex hai, isiliye multiple approximations use hote hain); KL controllers (original PPO me dynamic controllers the jo specific KL target karte the; most modern implementations static KL penalties use karti hain).

Policy gradient basics — pg_loss = −advantages × ratio

Simple implementation: pg_loss = -advantages * ratio, jahan ratio new policy ki probabilities ka reference model ke relative (per-token) probability ratio hai (aksar log-probability difference se compute hota hai). Teen cases: (1) Positive advantage — action expected value se behtar tha, reinforce karna hai; negative sign ki wajah se model logratio badhayega (positive logratio ka matlab hai model un tokens ko generate karne me zyada likely hai). (2) Negative advantage — action worse tha; loss positive hoga agar naya model zyada likely tha, isiliye model policy parameters ko aisa banayega ki completion kam likely ho. (3) Zero advantage — koi update nahi chahiye, loss zero hai.

Loss aggregation — 3 strategies

Per-token losses ℓi,t ko final scalar loss me aggregate kaise karna hai? Completion lengths |ai| aur batch size B given, teen main strategies hain:

StrategyFormulaEffect
1. Per-sequence normalization (standard GRPO; kuch PPO implementations)L = (1/B) Σi (1/|ai|) Σt ℓi,tHar sequence batch loss me equally contribute karti hai, length se farak nahi padta
2. Per-token normalization (DAPO)L = ΣiΣt ℓi,t / Σi|ai|Har token equally contribute karta hai; lambi sequences ka gradient par proportionally zyada influence
3. Fixed-length normalization (Dr. GRPO)L = (1/B) Σi (1/Lmax) Σt ℓi,tPer-token scale equalize karta hai, phir bhi lambi sequences zyada total gradient contribute karti hain kyunki unme zyada active tokens hain

Ye kyun matter karta hai — numbers se: do sequences lo — seq_1 losses [1,1,1,1,10] (5 tokens, mean 2.8) aur seq_2 losses [1×9, 10] (10 tokens, mean 1.9). Strategy 1 (per-sequence) me batch loss = (2.8+1.9)/2 = 2.35, aur crucially, chhoti sequence ke har token ko lambi sequence ke tokens se bada gradient milta hai. Strategy 2 (per-token) me batch loss = (14+19)/15 = 2.2, aur saare tokens ko equal gradient magnitude milta hai. Strategy 3 (fixed-length, Lmax=10) me chhoti sequence 1.4 aur lambi 1.9 contribute karti hai. Book ke code example me bhi yahi dikhta hai: masked_mean (Strategy 1) me short sequence ke per-token gradients 0.25 vs long ke 0.14; Strategies 2 aur 3 gradients equalize karte hain (0.1429 dono ke liye; token-level mean me 0.0909). Note: gradient accumulation use karne par results substantially vary kar sakte hain — gradients multiple minibatches par sum hote hain backward step se pehle, to shorter/longer sequences ke beech balance flip ho sakta hai. Practice me best strategy specific training setup par depend karti hai — aksar woh method prefer ki jaati hai jisme best numerical stability ya loss me least variance ho.

MDP vs bandit framing

Loss aggregation ka choice ek deeper distinction se judta hai: MDP (token-level) view — har token at ek action hai, state st running prefix hai; token-level advantages learned value function V(st) se compute hote hain (jaise GAE) aur KL penalties per token apply hote hain; PPO learned value network ke saath canonical example hai. Bandit (sequence-level) view — poori completion ek single action hai, ek scalar reward R ke saath; code me sequence-level advantage Aseq compute karke saare tokens par broadcast kiya jaata hai; RLOO aur GRPO-style advantages aksar isi bandit-style setting me use hote hain. DPO aur A-LoL jaise direct alignment methods bhi sequence-level objectives define karte hain, halanki woh policy-gradient estimators nahi hain. Note: kai GRPO implementations bandit-style advantage use karte hain aur loss me alag per-token KL term add karte hain, jabki kai PPO/RLOO implementations advantages compute karne se pehle KL ko reward me fold karte hain — dono conventions practice me exist karti hain.

Asynchronicity — actors aur learners

Policy-gradient algorithms ki default implementation on-policy execution hai — agent ke actions (generations) ko model update karne se pehle score kiya jaata hai. Theory me saare actions exactly on-policy hone chahiye, lekin practice me exact on-policy execution training ko substantially slow kar deta hai — aur perfect synchronization technically impossible hai. Isiliye language models ke saare recent empirical results theory ke proofs se thode bahar hain; practice me algorithms aur systems woh design kiye jaate hain jo asal me kaam karte hain.

Common solution: inference aur training ko alag GPU nodes par constantly chalana, efficient software ke saath — jaise Figure 6.3 ke bottom me dikhaya gaya hai. Popular open-source RL tools me common practice hai distributed process management library (jaise Ray) use karke policy-gradient learning loop aur inference loop ke beech information hand off karna, efficient inference engine (jaise vLLM) ke saath. In setups me RL steps lene wale GPUs ko "learners" aur language model se sample karne wale GPUs ko "actors" kehte hain. Primary challenges: training stable rakhna aur learning signal maintain karna.

Ye systems is presumption se design kiye gaye hain ki nearly on-policy data stable learning ke liye good enough hai. Generation aur update phases ko aasani se sync kiya jaa sakta hai taaki training system ke kisi bhi piece par idle compute na ho — learners se actors ko model weights pass karte hue. Reasoning models me 10K se 100K+ tokens per answer wali extremely long inference characteristics ki wajah se roll-outs generate karna far stronger bottleneck ban jaata hai. Ek common problem: synchronous RL infrastructure par reasoning models train karte waqt batch me ek prompt ka answer generate karne me substantially zyada time lag sakta hai (zyada tokens ya zyada tool calls se), jisse allocated compute ka zyada hissa idle rehta hai jab tak woh complete na ho. Is length mismatch ka doosra solution, sequence-level packing, hai — chhote samples ko batch ke andar clever masking ke saath stack karna taaki model se continued roll-outs enable hon aur length normalization samples ke across behtar distribute ho. Distributed RL infrastructure ki poori complexity is book ke scope se bahar hai, kyunki ye kai subtle issues paida kar sakti hai jo training slow kar dete hain ya instability cause karte hain.

Reasoning models ke emergence ke baad training aur inference loops ko fully off-policy banane me aur interest aaya hai — training batches policy gradient updates ke liye multiple instances se most recently completed roll-outs se bhare jaate hain. Fully asynchronous training RL training runs ko multiple datacenters across scale karna bhi enable karega, kyunki learner node aur actor ke beech weight syncs ke beech time badhane ka option milta hai.

PPO core code — 6 steps

Book PPO ka core loss computation deti hai (B = batch size, L = sequence length, G = generations ki sankhya): (1) rewards par KL penalty apply karo (rewards = rewards - beta * per_token_kl) aur value predictions lo; (2) advantages compute karo (advantages = rewards - values.detach()) aur normalize karo (mean 0, std 1); (3) ratio compute karo (ratio = exp(new_logps - old_logps)), eps jaise 0.2 se clip karo, pg_losses1 = -advantages * ratio, pg_losses2 = -advantages * clamp(ratio, 1-eps, 1+eps), pg_loss_max = max(pg_losses1, pg_losses2); (4) value function loss (vf_loss = 0.5 * (rewards - values)**2); (5) combine karo (per_token_loss = pg_loss_max + vf_coef * vf_loss), completion mask apply karke loss nikalo; (6) metrics log karo — clip_frac (kitne samples clip hue), approx_kl (0.5 × (logp diff)² ka mean), value_loss.

Key insight hai torch.max lena: kyunki hum negative loss minimize kar rahe hain, maximum lena zyada pessimistic gradient select karta hai — jo chhota policy update produce karta hai. Positive advantage par clipping policy ko action ki probability zyada aggressively badhane se rokta hai; negative advantage par doosri direction me over-correction rokta hai. Log-probability ratio clamp karke PPO policy ko training data generate karne wale version se kitna door drift kar sakti hai, use bound karta hai — bina explicit trust region computation ke.

1 gradient step simplification (Eq 6.38): PPO (aur GRPO) implementations bahut elegant ho jaate hain agar "number of gradient steps per sample" = 1 ho. Typical values 2–4 ya zyada hote hain. Main equations me "reference" policy previous parameters hoti hai — wahi jo completions generate karne ke liye use hui thi. Isiliye agar sirf ek gradient step liya jaaye, to πθ = πθold ho jaata hai, aur update rule reduce ho jaata hai: J(θ) = (1/G) Σ (πθ(ai|s) / [πθ(ai|s)]∇) × Ai − βDKL(πθ∥πref) — jahan []∇ stop gradient indicate karta hai. Isse second policy gradient aur clipping logic omit ki jaa sakti hai, optimizer standard policy gradient ke bahut kareeb aa jaata hai.

GRPO implementation — PPO se 3 differences

GRPO ka pseudocode: (1) group-wise reward statistics compute karo — mean aur std across generations for same prompt — advantages = (rewards − mean) / (std + 1e-4), unsqueeze karke (B*G, 1) shape; (2) PPO clipping objective wahi; (3) KL penalty loss me add karo (per_token_loss = pg_loss_max + beta * per_token_kl) — PPO reward se subtract karta hai, GRPO loss me add karta hai; (4) completion mask aur final loss; (5) metrics. Teen core differences: advantage computation group-relative normalization se hoti hai (learned value function baseline ke bajay); koi value network nahi — vf_loss aur uski complexity eliminate; KL penalty placement — GRPO KL ko loss me seedha add karta hai, reward se subtract karne ke bajay (standard implementation; aur versions exist karte hain). KL distance traditionally completion ke har token ke respect me compute hoti hai — reasoning training me shape [B, L, N] hoti hai (B = batch size, L = sequence length, N = completions per prompt).

RLOO vs GRPO code: RLOO ka advantage estimate GRPO ke bahut kareeb hai — completion reward relative to others for same question. TRL implementation se expanded: rewards ko (k, N) shape me reshape karo (k = completions per prompt, N = prompts), baseline = (sum − reward)/(k−1) — leave-one-out baseline — phir advantages = reward − baseline, flatten karo. Baaki implementation details doosre policy-gradient trade-offs follow karte hain.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 6

06.6Chapter 6 — Reinforcement Learning

6.3 Auxiliary Topics — GAE, double regularization, DAPO, VAPO

Policy-gradient algorithms ko master karne ke liye aur bhi countless considerations hain. Ye section long-tail complexities cover karta hai jo policy-gradient RL algorithm ko successfully deploy karne me aati hain.

Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) — bias-variance tradeoff

GAE advantage compute karne ka ek alternate method hai jo bias-variance tradeoff ko behtar balance karta hai. Traditional single-step advantage estimates zyada bias introduce kar sakte hain, jabki poori trajectories use karne se high variance hoti hai. GAE multi-step advantage estimates ka exponentially-weighted average compute karta hai, jahan λ hyperparameter bias-variance tradeoff control karta hai — single-step TD (λ = 0) se le kar full trajectory returns (λ = 1) tak; λ = 0.95 LLM fine-tuning ke liye common default hai.

TD residual define karo: δt = rt + γV(st+1) − V(st) (Eq 6.40). Phir GAE: ÂGAE(γ,λ)t = Σl=0..∞ (γλ)l δt+l (Eq 6.39/6.41) — future advantages ka exponential decay. Code backward loop me TD errors accumulate karta hai: delta = rewards[:, t] + gamma * not_done * next_v - values[:, t], gae = delta + gamma * lam * not_done * gae, advantages[:, t] = gae. Terminal tokens par not_done=0 bootstrapping rokta hai aur GAE accumulator reset karta hai, taaki har episode ke advantages independently compute hon. Final targets (advantages + values) value function ke regression targets hote hain, aur detached advantages policy loss ko weight karte hain — detached taaki policy updates value network se backpropagate na karen. RLHF me γ = 1.0 common hai kyunki episodes chhote token sequences hote hain jahan undiscounted credit assignment preferred hai.

Double Regularization — PPO clip + KL penalty, dono

Is chapter me do types ki regularization dekhi: ek PPO jaise algorithms me built-in step-size constraints, aur doosri KL divergence based distance penalty optimization ke start se relative. PPO me step-size cap karne wala objective "surrogate objective" kehlata hai. RLHF me PPO regularization updates ko kitna impact kar rahi hai, ye monitor karne ke liye kai popular implementations me clip fraction variable dekho — batch me samples ka percentage jahan gradients is regularizer se clip hote hain. Practice me language models ke saath PPO aur GRPO aksar sirf ek gradient step per batch ke saath chalaye jaate hain — matlab PPO-native regularization kabhi apply nahi hoti (clipping tabhi ho sakti hai jab policy batch ke andar substantially change ho) aur KL distance penalties predominate karte hain.

Further reading — naye algorithms

  • P3O (Pairwise Proximal Policy Optimization): pairwise data ko seedha PPO-style policy update me use karta hai, bina intermediate reward model seekhe.
  • CoPG (Contrastive Policy Gradient): off-policy policy-gradient algorithms jo aur asynchronous training enable kar sakte hain — direct alignment algorithm IPO aur vanilla policy gradient ka generalization; Command A model me use hua.
  • ReMax: language models ke liye design kiye gaye REINFORCE implementations — baseline normalization jo reward model inference se uncertainty ke sources ko accommodate karne ke liye design ki gayi hai.
  • MDPO (Mirror Descent Policy Optimization): kuch foundation models ne variants use kiye hain — Mirror Descent ek optimization method hai, seedha policy gradient algorithm nahi, lekin existing RL infrastructure me similarly substitute hota hai.
  • DAPO (Decoupled Clip and Dynamic sAmpling Policy Optimization): GRPO me 4 modifications propose karta hai taaki reasoning language models ko behtar suit kare, jahan long traces chahiye aur naye underutilized tokens ki probability badhani hai: (1) do alag clip hyperparameters, εlow aur εhigh, taaki logratio ke positive side par bade steps se behtar exploration ho; (2) dynamic sampling, jo saare samples hata deta hai jahan batch me sab samples ka reward = 0 ya reward = 1 hai (koi learning signal nahi); (3) per-token loss use karna; (4) bahut lambi samples par soft penalty, truncated answers se seekhne se bachne ke liye.
  • VAPO (Value-based Augmented PPO): DAPO ke optimizations (clip-higher, token-level policy-gradient, different length normalization) ko Value-Calibrated PPO ke insights ke saath combine karta hai — value function pretrain karna aur length-adaptive GAE — taaki GRPO ke relative value-based methods ka promise dikhaya jaa sake.
Chapter 6 ka takeaway: Policy gradient ka core hai log-derivative trick (Eq 6.11) + advantage (Eq 6.15). PPO ratio clip karke trust region banata hai (Eq 6.22–6.24). GRPO value function hatata hai aur group-relative advantage use karta hai (Eq 6.28). GSPO sequence-level ratios se token dropping fix karta hai; CISPO weights clip karke har token ka gradient bachata hai. Implementation me loss aggregation (per-sequence vs per-token vs fixed-length), asynchronicity (actors/learners, Ray + vLLM) aur GAE (λ = 0.95) decide karte hain ki training stable hogi ya nahi.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 6

07.1Chapter 7 — Reasoning & Inference-Time Scaling

Reasoning & Inference-Time Scaling — RLVR kya hai

2024 ke end aur 2025 me language models me sabse bada jump reasoning models se aaya — aise models jo jawab dene se pehle hazaaron tokens "sochte" hain. Iske peeche hai RLVR — Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards — jo RLHF jaisa hi hai, bas reward model ki jagah ek verification function hoti hai jo sahi jawab par reward 1 aur galat par 0 deti hai.

Cake wali analogy — RL ab cherry nahi, load-bearing hai

Ek mashhoor analogy kehti hai: agar intelligence ek cake hai, to self-supervised learning poora cake hai, supervised learning icing hai, aur reinforcement learning cherry hai. Reasoning models ne ye poora kar diya: pretraining cake hai, SFT icing hai, aur reasoning ke liye scale kiya hua RL cherry hai — ab ye cherry load-bearing ban chuka hai, matlab frontier training ka core hissa.

RLHF vs RLVR — scoring me farak

RLHF me reward model ko subjective cheezein judge karni padti hain — jaise "opportunity cost samjhao" wale jawab ki clarity, accuracy, completeness. RLVR me verification definite hoti hai: maths me extracted_answer == 77 → Reward = 1; code me unit tests — sab assertions pass to reward 1, koi fail to 0 (ya partial credit, jitne tests pass utna reward). Isi liye RLVR me zyada tar setups me learned reward model ki zaroorat hi nahi padti, halanki linear combination me use ho sakta hai.

Answer extraction ke tareeke

Maths me \boxed{} notation is liye popular hai — ek simple regex se final answer nikaala jaa sakta hai, chahe model wahan kaise bhi pahuncha ho. Doosre tareeke: "The answer is:" phrase, special tokens jaise <answer>, ya #### jaise delimiters. Code me unit tests natural verification hain.

RLVR naam kyun — RLGT kyun nahi

Originally is method ka naam RL with Ground Truth rewards (RLGT) rakhna tha. Lekin RLVR subtly alag hai: maths me single ground-truth answer hota hai, lekin code ya precise instruction following me verification function se check hota hai — multiple sahi solutions ho sakte hain. Core ye hai ki verifiable problems ki variety aur depth ho, exact solution pehle se pata ho ya na ho.

Pehle successful reasoning models

Is training ko pehle successfully deploy karne wale models the ek leading closed model (o1) aur ek open-weight model (DeepSeek R1). Uske baad poori industry ne is training process aur model style ko priority de di. Ye koi bilkul nayi RL setup nahi hai — stages ki reallocation aur alag behaviors ki priority hai. Reasoning models ne ek era laaya jahan RL training scale karna expected hai.

Thinking tokens ka example

"Write me a short poem about a goldfish" par ek normal model seedha poem deta hai. Reasoning model pehle bahut saare thinking tokens generate karta hai — imagery brainstorm karta hai ("gilded bowl", "crystal globe"), movement ke words sochta hai ("dart", "glide", "swirl"), theme decide karta hai (chhoti duniya vs freedom), rhyme aur rhythm check karta hai — phir final poem deta hai. Complex problems me reasoning stage hazaaron tokens tak ja sakta hai, is liye long-context models is behavior ke liye prerequisite the.

Core intuition — cycle repeat karo

Training ka core cycle bahut simple hai: (1) multiple questions ke multiple answers sample karo, (2) jo answers sahi hain unki taraf gradient steps lo, (3) repeat karo — wahi data baar-baar revisit karo. Hairani ki baat ye hai ki ye simple approach — careful data distribution aur stable infrastructure ke saath — models ko wahi questions revisit karke seekhne deti hai, aur improvement training questions se generalize karke unseen questions aur (kuch) domains tak pahunchta hai. Ye approach model ko behavior space me lightly search karne deti hai, aur RL algorithm un behaviors ki likelihood badhata hai jo sahi answers se correlated hain.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 7
← Previous6.3 Auxiliary Topics — GAE, double regularization, DAPO, VAPONext →Reasoning models ki origins — RL ab kaam kyun karta hai
07.2Chapter 7 — Reasoning & Inference-Time Scaling

Reasoning models ki origins — RL ab kaam kyun karta hai

Kai saal tak "RL doesn't work yet" wali takes aur reproducibility issues ke bawjood, field ne high-impact applications dhoondh liye — ChatGPT ka RLHF, DeepSeek R1 ka RLVR, chip design, video games, self-driving aur bhi. Reasoning models ka explosion 2025 me kyun hua, iske peeche kuch fundamental shifts hain.

Stability solve ho gayi

RL ki adoption ka limiting factor hamesha stability raha: pehla, learning fickle ho sakti hai — hamesha kaam nahi karti; doosra, training standard LM training se zyada brittle hai — loss spikes aur crashes zyada. Ab countless model releases verifiable rewards ke saath is style ki RL training use kar rahe hain, aur academic uptake bhi substantial hai. RL ke technical barriers to entry all-time low par hain.

Open-source tooling pehle se maujood

RLVR aur related techniques ke tools pehle se hain — jaise TRL, Open Instruct, veRL, OpenRLHF — jinme se kai RLHF ke earlier arc ki optimizations par bane hain. Tooling ki accessibility se research uptake badh raha hai, jo is chapter ko jaldi out of date bhi kar dega.

Capability threshold

Multiple resources kehte hain ki reasoning ke liye RL training sirf lagbhag 2024 ke baad ke leading models par viable thi — matlab models me pehle se ek level ki underlying capability chahiye thi, tabhi reasoning training possible hui.

RL training vs inference-time scaling

Inference-time scaling (test-time scaling) woh methods hain jo inference par zyada compute use karke downstream tasks par behtar karte hain — jaise value-guided sampling ya repeated random sampling with answer extraction. Ye DeepSeek R1 aur o1 se pehle bhi study kiye gaye the. RL training inference-time scaling laws use karne ka short path hai, lekin long-term me aur methods aayenge. RL se train kiye models zyada tokens per response generate karte hain, jo strongly correlated hai improved downstream performance se — halanki research ye bhi hai ki bina sequence length badhaaye performance improve ho. Ye early RLHF systems ke length-bias se bada shift hai, jahan human preference training ka side effect tha average response length badhna, marginal preference gains ke liye.

Future — reasoning se aage RLVR

Standard fine-tuning APIs me LoRA + SFT use hota hai: prompts aur completions do, model unhe match karna seekhta hai (1–2 epochs). RLVR answers match karne par focused hai: queries aur correct answers do, model sahi answers seekhta hai — aur ye wahi few data points par sau ya hazaar epochs tak karta hai, taaki model ko naye behaviors seekhne ka time mile. Ise aise dekho: base model me sparingly kaam karne wale positive behaviors ko robust behaviors me reinforce karna.

RL training ka scope badhta ja raha hai: o1 aur R1 se sabse bada scientific takeaway ye tha ki valuable behaviors train karne ke aur bhi tareeke hain. Jitne zyada doors researchers aur engineers ke liye khulte hain, AI ki general trajectory ke baare me utna optimism hona chahiye.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 7

07.3Chapter 7 — Reasoning & Inference-Time Scaling

Reasoning training methods — STaR se lekar Table 7.1 tak

o1 aur R1 se pehle bhi verifiable domains par models train karne ki substantial koshish hui thi — STaR, TRICE, VinePPO — lekin unki methodologies R1 jitni scale nahi hui, ya overall performance sacrifice karke maths/coding badhaayi. Uske baad aayi Table 7.1 — 2025 ke notable reasoning models ki summary — aur common practices ki list.

Pre-o1/R1 kaam

  • STaR (2022–23): ground-truth reward signals se chain-of-thought reasoning encourage karta hai; policy gradient ko approximate karta hai, lekin samples ko alag filter karta hai aur log-probability ki jagah cross-entropy use karta hai. Quiet-STaR model ko answer se pehle tokens generate karne deta hai.
  • TRICE: traces generate karke Markov chain Monte Carlo inspired expectation maximization se optimize karta hai.
  • VinePPO: PPO-based algorithm, binary rewards for math correctness, GSM8K aur MATH par training — modern reasoning models ke sabse kareeb.
  • Code execution feedback: code execution ko feedback signal banakar training, aur theorem proving ke liye verifier feedback (RLVF).
  • Tülu 3: simple PPO trainer se sahi answers wale completions ko reward — sabse important, model ki overall performance broad evaluations par maintain rakhte hue. Binary rewards STaR ke iterative approach ya Quiet-STaR ke log-likelihood rewards se contrast karte hain.

Table 7.1 — notable reasoning models (2025)

Book me 2025 ke 25+ reasoning models ki table hai (date, model, organization, open weights, open data/process, notes). Kuch highlights:

DateModelNotes

2025-03-31Open-Reasoner-ZeroBase model RL ki fully open replication; Yes/Yes

2025-05-12INTELLECT-2Pehla publicly documented globally-decentralized RL training run; Yes/Yes

Table me aur bhi hain: Hunyuan-TurboS (Mamba-Transformer MoE, adaptive long/short CoT), MiMo-VL (multi-modal), OpenThoughts (1.2M-example dataset distilled from QwQ-32B), K2-Think (32B, fully open), LongCat-Flash-Thinking (560B MoE, staged recipe), Ring-1T (trillion-scale thinking model), Nemotron 3 Nano (30B-A3B MoE, 25T tokens pretrain).

Common practices (7.2.3)

  • Offline difficulty filtering: Model sirf un examples se seekh sakta hai jahan gradient ho. Agar starting model kisi problem ko 100% ya 0% solve karta hai, to completions ke beech koi gradient nahi. Is liye large-scale RL se pehle problems ko filter karo — sirf woh jinhe starting model 20–80% time solve karta hai. Method: har prompt par N (jaise 16) completions sample karo, verify karo kitne percent sahi hain. Use kiya: Seed-Thinking 1.5, Open Reasoner Zero, Phi-4, INTELLECT-2, MiMo RL, Skywork OR-1.
  • Per-batch online filtering / difficulty curriculum: Training ke dauraan batch me questions filter karo, mushkil problems baad ke liye bachao, ya data schedulers use karo. Use kiya: Kimi 1.5, Magistral, Llama-Nemotron, INTELLECT-2, MiMo-RL, Hunyuan-TurboS.
  • KL penalty hatao: RL runs lambe hone aur reward function ke over-optimization-prone na hone par kai models ne KL penalty hata di — model aur explore kar sakta hai. Use kiya: RAGEN, Magistral, OpenReasonerZero, Skywork OR-1.
  • Relaxed policy-gradient clipping: DAPO jaise GRPO variations ne two-sided clipping modify ki taaki exploration behtar ho; clipping imperfect rewards par spurious learning signals bhi de sakti hai. Use kiya: RAGEN, Magistral, INTELLECT-2.
  • Off-policy / fully asynchronous updates: Completions ki length variance badhne par compute idle baithta hai — asynchronous updates ya batch arrangement se throughput badhao. Use kiya: Seed-Thinking 1.5, INTELLECT-2.
  • Additional format rewards: <think>...</think> format follow karne par chhota reward, taaki reasoning predictable ho. Use kiya: DeepSeek R1, OpenReasonerZero, Magistral, Skywork OR-1.
  • Language consistency rewards: Reasoning ke dauraan language na badle — multilingual models ke liye. Use kiya: DeepSeek R1, Magistral.
  • Length penalties: Overthinking mitigate karne ya stability ke liye — jaise Kimi 1.5 target length progressively extend karta hai, INTELLECT-2 chhota length penalty chalata hai. Sequence length progressively extend karne se model pehle limited thinking budget me effectively reason karna seekhta hai, phir longer training me woh behaviors efficiently use karta hai.
  • Loss normalization: GRPO ke per-group normalization se length/difficulty bias aata hai — is liye Magistral ya MiMo ne losses/advantages ko group level ki jagah batch level par normalize kiya.
  • Parallel test-time compute scaling: Multiple parallel rollouts se answers combine karo — sabse naive: majority vote (DeepSeek R1, Phi-4). Advanced: scoring model se best answer select karo — open recipes me abhi adopt nahi hua (June 2025 tak), lekin ek leading announcement me mention aur ek generalist reward model me use hua.

Ancillary capabilities bachana

  • Text-only reasoning se multimodal performance badhti hai: Magistral, MiMo-VL — multimodal training ke baad text-only reasoning training se multimodal performance improve hoti hai.
  • Toggleable reasoning: Llama-Nemotron, Nemotron Nano, Qwen 3, SmolLM 3 — system prompt (kabhi length-controlled RL ke saath) se thinking on/off toggle. Kuch open models low-medium-high reasoning effort system prompt me set karte hain.
Honest caveat: Book khud kehta hai — ye examples sirf known implementations ka subset hain, optimal recipe ka final proclamation nahi. Kisi paper ne technique use ki ho aur mention na ki ho, to woh list me nahi hogi.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 7
