12.1Chapter 12 — Synthetic Data

Synthetic Data — kyun synthetic data kaam karta hai

RLHF deeply rooted hai models par human influence rakhne ke idea me. Jab pehle models RLHF se successfully train hue, human data hi ek viable tareeka tha models ko is tarah improve karne ka. Humans hi ek tareeka the high enough quality responses banane ka, aur reliable, specific feedback data collect karke reward models train karne ka. Jaise AI models behtar hue, ye assumption rapidly break ho gayi. Synthetic data — jo far cheaper aur iterate karne me aasan hai — ne RLHF ko center of attention se broader "post-training" ki taraf badhne diya.

Model collapse — criticism aur reality

Synthetic data ki ek common criticism hai model collapse — idea ki model ki apni generations par repeatedly train karne se effective training distribution progressively narrow ho jaati hai. Jaise diversity girti hai, rare facts aur styles underrepresented ho jaate hain, aur chhoti mistakes iterations ke across amplify ho sakti hain, leading to worse generalization. Practice me ye failures sabse zyada unfiltered, repetitive, single-model outputs par self-training se associated hain; real/human data mix karna, diverse teachers use karna, deduplication, aur strong quality filters collapse regime ko largely avoid kar dete hain. Aaj ki frontier training pipelines ke liye evidence suggest karta hai ki synthetic data scale par use kiya jaa sakta hai aur karna chahiye, bina collapse story ke strongest versions ke catastrophic regressions ke.

Leading models ko synthetic data chahiye

Modern post-training me synthetic data training ke bahut se pieces encompass karta hai — language models use hote hain naye training prompts generate karne ke liye seed examples se, existing prompts modify karne ke liye, prompts ke completions generate karne ke liye, preference data banane ke liye AI feedback provide karne ke liye, completions filter karne ke liye, aur bahut kuch. Synthetic data post-training ki key hai.

Synthetic data ke is extent tak impactful hone ki ability GPT-4 class models ke saath emerge hui. Early language models, jaise Llama 2 aur GPT-3.5-Turbo, data pipelines generate ya supervise karne me reliable nahi the. 1–2 saal me language models answers generate karne me humans se far superior ho gaye. GPT-3.5 se GPT-4 class models ki transition me LLM-as-a-judge tasks karne ki ability bhi emerge hui. GPT-4 ya behtar models kisi content ke baare me feedback ya scores generate karne me far zyada robust aur consistent hain.

Impactful synthetic datasets — timeline aur scale

ChatGPT ke end of 2022 release ke baad se numerous impactful synthetic datasets aaye — kuch include: UltraFeedback, pehla prominent synthetic preference dataset jisne DPO revolution kickstart ki; Stanford Alpaca, 2023 me pehle chat-style fine-tuning datasets me se ek; skill-focused (math, code, instruction-following) synthetic datasets Tülu 3 me; ya OpenThoughts 3 aur 2025 me thinking models train karne ke liye bahut se doosre synthetic reasoning datasets. Aaj industry-grade post-training start karne ke canonical references me Tülu 3 ya OpenThoughts 3 jaise datasets involve hain, jahan quickstart guides aksar Alpaca jaise chhote, simpler datasets se start karte hain far faster training ki wajah se.

Ek bada change dataset size se bhi related hai — fine-tuning datasets prompts ki sankhya me badhe hain: Alpaca 52K hai, OpenThoughts aur Tülu 3 1M+ samples hain, aur responses ki length bhi badhi hai. Longer responses aur zyada prompts ka result: Alpaca dataset lagbhag 10M training tokens ka hai, Tülu lagbhag 50X bada hai — about 500M tokens — aur OpenThoughts 3 usse bhi bada hai — order of 10B tokens.

Kahan synthetic jeeta, kahan human abhi bhi chahiye

Is transition ke dauraan, synthetic data ne human data ko pipeline bhar me uniformly replace nahi kiya hai. Instruction data (SFT) ke liye synthetic generation largely jeet gaya hai — stronger models se distillation ab scale par zyada tar human writers se higher quality completions deta hai (kuch exception hardest frontier reasoning problems me). Preference data ke liye picture zyada mixed hai: academic work dikhata hai ki synthetic preference data comparably perform karta hai, phir bhi frontier labs human preference data ko competitive moat treat karte hain. Evaluation ke liye split alag flavor leta hai: LLM-as-a-judge model outputs score karna cost-effectively scale karta hai, lekin underlying benchmarks aur ground-truth labels abhi bhi human creation chahiye. Pattern ye hai: synthetic data wahan dominate karta hai jahan models human reliability se exceed karte hain, jabki humans capability frontiers par, ground truth establish karne ke liye, aur training guide karne ke liye essential rehte hain.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 12
← PreviousBias aur open questions — data collection me kya dekhna haiNext →Distillation — teacher se student tak
12.2Chapter 12 — Synthetic Data

Distillation — teacher se student tak

Distillation synthetic data ke role par discussion ka sabse powerful form raha hai language models me. Distillation term deep learning literature se teacher-student knowledge distillation ki technical definition se aata hai. Colloquially, distillation ka matlab hai stronger model ke outputs use karke chhote model ko train karna.

Post-training me distillation ke do common forms

  1. Data engine ke roop me: Post-training process ke wide swaths me use — instructions ke liye completions, preference data (ya Constitutional AI), ya RL ke liye verification.
  2. Specific skills transfer karna: Stronger model se weaker model ko specific skills transfer karna — aksar mathematical reasoning ya coding jaise specific skills ke liye.

Pehli strategy popularity me badhi hai jaise language models answers likhne me humans se zyada reliable hue hain variety of tasks par. GPT-4 class models ne iska scope expand kiya — math aur code jaise complex tasks ke liye stronger models ki distillation use karne tak. Yahan distillation motivate karta hai ek model suite rakhna jahan aksar laboratory ek bada internal model train karegi — jaise ek leading lab ka sabse bada model ya doosre lab ka sabse bada model — jo publicly release nahi hota aur sirf internally use hota hai stronger models banane ke liye. Open models ke saath, common practice hai closed API models se training data distill karke chhote, openly available weights me daalna. Iske andar, teacher model se high-quality prompts curate karna aur responses filter karna crucial hai performance maximize karne ke liye.

Specific skills chhote language models me transfer karna wahi principles use karta hai — training ke liye best possible data pao. Yahan bahut se papers ne study kiya hai stronger models se limited datasets use karke alignment, mathematical reasoning aur test-time scaling improve karna.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 12
← PreviousSynthetic Data — kyun synthetic data kaam karta haiNext →AI Feedback (RLAIF) — human aur AI feedback ka balance
12.3Chapter 12 — Synthetic Data

AI Feedback (RLAIF) — human aur AI feedback ka balance

RLHF me growth ke explosion ke turant baad, RL from AI Feedback (RLAIF) emerge hua ek alternative approach ke roop me — jahan AIs human data wale pipeline ke hisse ko approximate karke experimentation ya progress accelerate kar sakte hain. AI feedback, generally, techniques ka bada set hai kisi input ki quality explain karne wala data use karke augment ya generate karne ke liye — jo alag training approaches ya evaluations me use ho sakta hai — jo pairwise preferences se start hua. RLAIF use karne ki bahut si motivations hain — human feedback ko entirely replace karna ya augment karna. RLHF process ke andar, AI feedback sabse zyada known hai preference data collection aur related reward model training phase me apne role ke liye (jiska Constitutional AI ek certain type ki implementation hai).

Jaise AI feedback mature hua, uske applications human preference labels replace karne se aage expand hue. Wahi LLM-as-a-judge infrastructure jisne cheaper preference data collection enable ki, usne scalable evaluation bhi enable ki (Chapter 17), aur haal me rubric-based rewards jo RL training ko domains tak extend karte hain jahan verifiable answers nahi hain — ek frontier jo is chapter me baad me explore ki gayi hai.

Cost — $1+ vs $0.01 se kam

AI models kisi specific quantity ka feedback generate karne me humans se far cheaper hain — ek single piece of human preference data ki cost likhne ke time par order of $1 ya higher hai (ya per prompt $10 se bhi upar), jabki frontier AI model se AI feedback, jaise ek leading model, ki cost $0.01 se kam hai. Iske aage, human labor ki cost roughly constant reh rahi hai, jabki in tasks par leading models ki performance badhti ja rahi hai aur price-per-performance girta ja raha hai. Ye cost difference RLHF methods ke saath experimentation ka market ek poori population ke liye khol deta hai jo pehle priced out thi.

Tradeoffs — price se aage

Price ke alawa, AI feedback human feedback se alag performance tradeoffs introduce karta hai, jo broader literature me abhi investigate ho rahe hain. AI feedback evaluation me apne role me far zyada predominant hai — kyunki uski low price use bade-scale tasks ke across use karne deti hai jahan human data ki cost (ya time delay) impractical hoti. Ye saare topics deeply intertwined hain — AI feedback data human data ko kabhi fully replace nahi karega, evaluation ke liye bhi nahi, aur evaluation ke liye AI feedback ki quantity training se far outperform karegi kyunki evaluate karne wale log train karne walon se far zyada hain.

Balance kahan hai — nuanced picture

Exact domains aur applications — chat, safety, reasoning, mathematics, etc. — jahan AI feedback data human data se outperform karta hai, woh completely establish nahi hue hain. Kuch early RLAIF kaam dikhata hai ki AI feedback human data ko completely replace kar sakta hai, effective replacement ke roop me tout karte hue — khaas taur par jab sirf chat tasks par evaluate kiya jaaye. Early literature ChatGPT ke baad RLHF study karne wali narrow evaluation suites par thi — helpful assistants ki "alignment" par focus. Baad ka kaam zyada nuanced picture leta hai, jahan broader evaluation set par optimal equilibrium — kuch reasoning tasks include karke — challenging data-points ka ek set humans ko accurately label karne ke liye route karna hai, jabki zyada tar data AI feedback ke liye bheja jaata hai. Human aur AI feedback data ke beech balance par focused studies broad domains ke across nahi hain, lekin bahut se technical reports dikhate hain ki RLHF generally broad suite of evaluations ko improve kar sakta hai — kuch DPO use karte hain, jaise Tülu 3 aur Olmo 3, ya SmolLM 3, aur doosre online RLHF pipelines use karte hain, jaise ek chip company ka kaam jo human preference data (ek data vendor se) aur LLM-based feedback ka mix use karta hai (HelpSteer line of work ke through): Nemotron Nano 3, Nemotron-Cascade, ya Llama-Nemotron reasoning models.

Rule of thumb — high-noise/low-bias vs low-noise/high-bias

1. Human data high-noise aur low-bias hai: Matlab collection aur filtering harder ho sakti hai, lekin jab wrangle kar lo to bahut reliable signal milega.
2. Synthetic preference data low-noise aur high-bias hai: Matlab AI feedback data se start karna aasan hoga, lekin model par tricky, unintended second-order effects ho sakte hain jo data me systematically represent hote hain.

Overall: jahan AI feedback aur related methods field ke liye obviously extremely useful hain, ye clear hai ki human data in cheaper alternatives se completely replace nahi hua hai. Bahut si hypotheses hain, lekin study nahi hua hai ki kya human data real-world product settings me models ka finer control deta hai ya newer training methods jaise character training ke liye (emerging set of techniques jo model ki personality precisely control karne dete hain, Chapter 18 me cover). Shuru karne walon ke liye AI feedback pehla attempt hona chahiye, lekin larger operations tak scale karne wali pipelines ke liye human feedback include karne ka eventual transition likely hai.

RLAIF vs Constitutional AI — confusion clear karo

RLAIF term ek paper me introduce hua tha — Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback — jisne AI community me initial confusion create ki dono methods ke beech relationship ko lekar (Constitutional AI aur AI Feedback). CAI paper ke release aur RLAIF ke formalization ke baad se, RLAIF post-training aur RLHF literatures ke andar ek default method ban gaya hai — examples itne hain ki easily enumerate nahi kiye jaa sakte. Relationship aise samajhna chahiye: CAI woh example tha jisne RLAIF ke broader field ko kickstart kiya.

Specific LLMs for judgement (12.2.2)

Jaise RLAIF methods prevalent hue, bahut ne wonder kiya: kya responses generate karne wale aur critiques ya ratings generate karne wale models same hone chahiye? LLM-as-a-judge ki calibration question me aayi hai. Kai works ne dikhaya hai ki LLMs inconsistent evaluators hain aur apne responses ko doosre models ke responses se prefer karte hain (self-preference bias). Iske result me bahut ne pucha: kya solution ye hoga ki labeling task ke liye ek separate model train kiya jaaye? Multiple models release hue hain frontier models ko data labeling tool ke roop me substitute karne ke goal se — jaise critic models Shepherd aur CriticLLM, ya response performance evaluate karne wale models Auto-J, Prometheus, Prometheus 2, ya Prometheus-Vision — lekin woh documented training recipes me widely adopt nahi hue hain. Kuch ko lagta hai repeated sampling se inference scale karna, self-refinement, ya tournament ranking true judgement ka behtar estimate ya higher-quality preference pairs deta hai. Doosri calibration techniques generation aur judgement capabilities ko co-evolve karti hain. Accepted hai ki biases exist karte hue bhi, leading language models is task ke liye extensively train kiye jaate hain — kyunki ye AI labs ki internal operations ke liye needed hai aur customers extensively use karte hain — to generally apna judge train karne ki zaroorat nahi hai, jab tak aapke task me substantial private information involve na ho jo public internet par expose nahi hai.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 12

12.4Chapter 12 — Synthetic Data

Constitutional AI — principles se synthetic data

Constitutional AI (CAI) — jo ek leading lab apne Claude models me use karta hai — RLHF training ke liye synthetic data ka sabse pehla documented, large-scale use hai. CAI do tareekon se synthetic data generate karta hai.

Do tareeke

  1. Instruction-tuned data ki critiques: Principles ke set ko follow karne ke liye — jaise "Is the answer encouraging violence?" ya "Is the answer truthful?" Jab model questions ke answers generate karta hai, woh answer ko constitution ke principles ki list ke against check karta hai, time ke saath answer refine karta hai. Phir woh model ko resulting dataset par fine-tune karte hain.
  2. Pairwise preference data generate karna: Language model use karke answer karna kaunsi completion behtar thi, constitution se ek random principle ka context de kar (principle-guided reward models par research jaisa). Phir RLHF normal jaise proceed karta hai synthetic data ke saath — isi liye RLAIF naam.

Largely, CAI apne doosre hisse — preference data — ke liye known hai, lekin instruction data ke liye introduce kiye gaye methods general data filtering aur synthetic data generation methods me post-training bhar use hote hain.

Formalization

CAI ko formalize kiya jaa sakta hai: human-written principles ke set — constitution C — ko employ karke, ek separate LLM use kiya jaata hai artificial preference aur instruction data generate karne ke liye jo fine-tuning me use hota hai. Constitution C written principles ka set hai jo critique phase ke dauraan focus karne wale specific aspects indicate karta hai. Instruction data curate kiya jaata hai ek principle ci ∈ C ko repeatedly sample karke aur model se puch kar ki woh apna latest output yi ko prompt x ke liye revise kare taaki woh ci se align ho. Isse instruction variants ki series {y0, y1, …, yn} milti hai critique ke liye use kiye gaye principles {c0, c1, …, cn−1} se. Final data point prompt x hai saath me final completion yn, kisi n ke liye.

Preference data similar, lekin simpler tareeke se construct kiya jaata hai — C ke principles ke subset ko feedback model ke liye context banakar. Feedback model ko prompt x, principles ka set {c0, …, cn}, aur do completions y0 aur y1 present kiye jaate hain jo answers (A) aur (B) ke roop me label kiye gaye hain, previous RLHF dataset se. Naya datapoint generate hota hai language model se select karwakar ki kaunsa output (A) ya (B) higher quality hai aur stated principle se zyada aligned hai. Earlier models me ye prompt karke kiya jaa sakta tha "The answer is:" aur dekh kar ki kaunsa logit (A ya B) higher probability rakhta hai, lekin zyada commonly ab ek model se handle kiya jaata hai jo apni reasoning explain karega aur phir answer select karega — commonly generative reward model ke roop me refer kiya jaata hai.

Further reading on CAI (12.3.1)

  • Model Spec: Ek leading lab ne Model Spec release kiya hai — document jo unke models ke liye intended behavior state karta hai — aur kaha hai ki woh alignment ke methods explore kar rahe hain jahan model document ko seedha reference karta hai (CAI ka close peer samjha jaa sakta hai). Us lab ne apne reasoning models ko Deliberative Alignment naam ki method se train kiya hai — safety ya behavior policies ko reference karte hue model ko align karne ke liye.
  • Constitution updates: Ek leading lab CAI use karna continue kar raha hai apne model training me — constitution update karte hue aur experiment karte hue ki population collectives principles par kaise converge karte hain aur ye model behavior ko kaise badalta hai jab woh principles khud banate hain aur phir lab ke saath share karte hain models train karne ke liye.
  • Open-source replications: Open-source community ne CAI ki replications explore ki hain open datasets par apply karke aur LMs ke beech dialogue data banane ke explorations ke liye.
  • Doosra principle-driven kaam: Kuch kaam principles ko reward models ke liye context banakar use karte hain (Dromedary models train karne ke liye use hua), kuch principles use karte hain RLHF process me human judgments ki accuracy improve karne ke liye, kuch reward model train karte hain jo inference time par apne principles generate kare aur final score deliver karne ke liye use kare, aur kuch principle-following ko mutual information maximization problem ke roop me formulate karte hain jo pretrained model bina labels ke seekh sakta hai.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 12
← PreviousAI Feedback (RLAIF) — human aur AI feedback ka balanceNext →Rubrics — AI feedback se RL training (verifiable answers ke bina)
12.5Chapter 12 — Synthetic Data

Rubrics — AI feedback se RL training (verifiable answers ke bina)

AI feedback ka training me role late 2024 aur 2025 me badha, jab field RLVR scale karne ke avenues dhoondh rahi thi (Chapter 7). Rubrics ka idea emerge hua — un prompts ke liye nearly-verifiable criteria paane ka tareeka jinke clearly verifiable answers nahi hain. Isse model multiple answers generate karke (RL se) best answers ki taraf update kar sakta hai. Ye idea is chapter me discuss kiye gaye doosre methods se closely related hai, aur likely tab kaam karna shuru hua jab LLM judges aur synthetic data practices industry bhar me improve hue. Ab rubrics as rewards ke saath RL scientific reasoning ya factuality jaise skills me meaningful improvements dene me established hai.

Example rubric — museum exhibit prompt

Prompt: "As a museum curator, can you suggest five obscure artifacts that would be perfect for a 'Mysteries of the Ancient World' exhibit? Each artifact should come from a different culture and time period, with a brief description of their historical significance and mysterious origins. These artifacts should leave visitors wondering about the secrets and lost knowledge of our past."

Rubric (10 items):

  1. Response me exactly five distinct artifacts hain, jaise request kiya gaya. [Hard Rule]
  2. Har artifact alag culture aur time period se hai. [Hard Rule]
  3. Har artifact ki historical significance ki brief description hai. [Hard Rule]
  4. Har artifact ki mysterious origins ya unexplained aspects ki brief description hai. [Hard Rule]
  5. Response me intrigue aur mystery ka sense hai jo exhibit ke theme se align karta hai. [Hard Rule]
  6. Response information ko well-organized aur coherent manner me clearly aur accurately communicate karta hai. [Principle]
  7. Response precision aur clarity dikhata hai unnecessary ya irrelevant details avoid karke. [Principle]
  8. Response informative aur engaging language use karta hai jo curiosity aur critical thinking stimulate kare. [Principle]
  9. Response thoughtful selection dikhata hai — har example overall theme me uniquely contribute karta hai bina redundancy ke. [Principle]
  10. Response style aur format me consistency maintain karta hai readability aur comprehension enhance karne ke liye. [Principle]

[Hard Rule] aur [Principle] specific tags hain kisi feedback ki priority denote karne ke liye. Importance indicate karne ke doosre methods bhi use ho sakte hain, jaise simple priority numbers.

Rubric generation — kaise banti hai

Rubric generation generally training data me per-prompt ki jaati hai, jo preparation me meaningful synthetic data costs accumulate karti hai. Isse alleviate karne ke liye, ek general rubric aksar per-domain starting point ke roop me apply ki jaati hai, aur phir per-prompt fine-grained rubric scores ek supervising language model assign karta hai training ke liye feedback guide karne ke liye.

Ek science task ke liye rubric generate karne ka example prompt: "You are an expert rubric writer for science questions in the domains of Biology, Physics, and Chemistry. Your job is to generate a self-contained set of evaluation criteria ('rubrics') for judging how good a response is to a given question in one of these domains. Rubrics can cover aspects such as factual correctness, depth of reasoning, clarity, completeness, style, helpfulness, and common pitfalls. Each rubric item must be fully self-contained so that non-expert readers need not consult any external information. Inputs: question (full question text), reference_answer (ideal answer, key facts aur explanations ke saath). Total items: question complexity ke basis par 7–20 rubric items choose karo. Har rubric item me exactly three keys hone chahiye: (1) title (2–4 words); (2) description — ek sentence jo apne category prefix se start hoti hai, explicitly state karte hue kya dekhna hai; (3) weight — Essential/Important/Optional ke liye 1–5 (5 = most important); Pitfall ke liye −1 ya −2."

Categories aur example items

  • Essential Criteria: Critical facts ya safety checks; omission response ko invalidate kar deta hai. Example: "States that in the described closed system, the total mechanical energy (kinetic plus potential) before the event equals the total mechanical energy after the event."
  • Important Criteria: Key reasoning ya completeness; quality ko strongly affect karta hai. Example: numerical energy values ko har stage ke liye break down karna, dikhate hue ki initial kinetic + initial potential energy equals final kinetic + final potential energy.
  • Optional Criteria: Nice-to-have style ya extra depth. Example: concrete example dena, jaise pendulum kinetic aur potential energy ke beech convert karta hai.
  • Pitfall Criteria: Common mistakes ya omissions; woh cheezein highlight karo jo aksar miss hoti hain. Example: mention nahi karna ki frictional ya air-resistance losses negligible assume kiye gaye hain conservation of mechanical energy apply karte time.

Format notes: answer choices refer karte time explicitly kaho "Identifies (A)", "Identifies (B)", etc. Agar clear conclusion required ho (jaise "The final answer is (B)"), to uske liye Essential Criteria include karo. Agar reasoning final answer se pehle aani chahiye, to uske liye Important Criteria include karo. Agar brevity valued ho, to conciseness ke baare me Optional Criteria include karo. Output: JSON array of rubric objects. Har object me exactly three keys — title, description, weight. Question ya reference_answer ke bade blocks copy mat karo. Har description apne category prefix se start honi chahiye, aur koi extra keys allowed nahi hain. Reference answer ideal response hai lekin necessarily exhaustive nahi — use sirf guidance ke roop me use karo.

Ek simpler rubric prompt

SYSTEM:
You generate evaluation rubrics for grading an assistant's response to a user prompt.
Rubric design rules:
- Each criterion must be atomic (one thing), objective as possible, and written
  so a grader can apply it consistently.
- Avoid redundant/overlapping criteria; prefer criteria that partition different
  failure modes.
- Make criteria self-contained (don't rely on unstated context).
- Include an importance weight for each criterion.
Output format (JSON only):
{
  "initial_reasoning": "<brief rationale for what matters for this prompt>",
  "rubrics": [
    {
       "reasoning": "<why this criterion matters>",
       "criterion": "<clear, testable criterion>",
       "weight": <integer 1-10>
    }, ...
  ]
}
USER:
User prompt: {prompt}
Generate the rubric JSON now.

Jaise dekh sakte ho, prompts bahut detailed ho sakte hain aur training setup ke liye tune kiye jaate hain. Rubrics ke saath RL training early applications se aage evolve hoti rahegi — instruction following, deep research, deep research agents evaluate karna, ya long-form generation tak.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 12

13.1Chapter 13 — Tool Use & Function Calling

Tool Use & Function Calling — models tools kaise use karte hain

Language models ka tools use karna unki capabilities expand karne ka natural tareeka hai — khaas taur par high-precision tasks ke liye jahan external tools me information hoti hai, ya agents ke liye jo complex web systems se interact karte hain. Tool-use ek skill hai jo language models ko train karke sikhayi jaati hai — RLHF aur book me present ki gayi saari doosri methods se refine ki jaa sakti hai.

Ek simple sawal — "Who is the president today?"

Bina tools ke language model is sawal ka jawab dene me mushkil hogi — pretraining data ki knowledge cutoff ki wajah se. Lekin ek search query se ye readily accessible information hai. Tools doosri weakness bhi mitigate karte hain: language models ki probabilistic, generative nature. Example: pi ko 50 digits tak print karna (memory se recite karke hallucination risk liye bina). Tools wala model code execution se precise answer de sakta hai:

from decimal import Decimal, getcontext
getcontext().prec = 60
def compute_pi():
    # Chudnovsky algorithm for computing pi
    C = 426880 * Decimal(10005).sqrt()
    K, M, X, L, S = 0, 1, 1, 13591409, Decimal(13591409)
    for i in range(1, 100):
        M = M * (K**3 - 16*K) // ((i)**3)
        K += 12
        L += 545140134
        X *= -262537412640768000
        S += Decimal(M * L) / X
    return C / S
print(str(compute_pi())[:52])

Output: 3.14159265358979323846264338327950288419716939937510

Terms jo interchangeably use hote hain — farak samjho

  • Tool use: model ek structured request emit karta hai (tool name aur arguments); orchestrator tool execute karta hai; results context me append hote hain; model generate karna continue karta hai.
  • Function calling: tool use jahan arguments ko declared schema (usually JSON Schema) conform karna hota hai ek set of functions ke liye — reliable parsing aur validation enable karta hai.
  • Code execution: tool use ka special case jahan "tool" ek code interpreter hai (jaise Python); results tool output ke roop me return hote hain.

Ek AI model kisi bhi external tool ko special tokens output karke use karta hai jo certain endpoint trigger karte hain. Ye kuch bhi ho sakte hain — highly specific tools (jaise kisi jagah ka weather return karne wala function) se lekar code interpreters ya search engines tak jo complex behaviors ke fundamental building blocks hain.

Origins — 2015 se aaj tak

"Tool use" term ki exact origin clear nahi hai, lekin idea post-ChatGPT world se bahut pehle ka hai. Early examples circa 2015 me modern language models se pehle ke systems banane ki koshish thi — jaise Neural Programmer-Interpreters (NPI), "a recurrent and compositional neural network that learns to represent and execute programs." Jaise language models popular hue, bahut se subfields external capabilities ke integrations se performance boost kar rahe the: weights ke bahar ki information paane ke liye retrieval augmented generation ya web browsing use karte the. Uske turant baad, doosre language models ko programs ya tools ke saath integrate karna explore kar rahe the.

Jaise field mature hui, models ko underlying language modeling me vast improvements ke alawa zyada complex abilities mili. Example: ToolFormer "a calculator, a Q&A system, two different search engines, a translation system, and a calendar" use kar sakta tha. Uske turant baad, Gorilla 1,645 APIs use karne ke liye train hua (PyTorch Hub, TensorFlow Hub v2, aur HuggingFace se) aur uska evaluation APIBench popular Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard ka foundation bana. Tab se called actions ki diversity substantially badh gayi hai.

Aaj tool-use models regular language model interactions ke saath deeply intertwine ho gaye hain. Model Context Protocol (MCP) ek common formatting ke roop me emerge hua language models ko external data sources (ya tools) se connect karne ke liye. Stronger models aur behtar formats ke saath, tool-use language models bahut si situations me use hote hain — popular applications ke andar productivity copilots (jaise ek leading office suite ya workspace suite), scientific domains, medical domains, coding agents (jaise do leading coding tools), databases ke saath integrations, aur bahut se autonomous workflows.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 13
← PreviousRubrics — AI feedback se RL training (verifiable answers ke bina)Next →Generation me tool calls interweave karna — format aur orchestration
13.2Chapter 13 — Tool Use & Function Calling

Generation me tool calls interweave karna — format aur orchestration

Function calling agents ko data bahut similarly present kiya jaata hai doosre post-training stages ki tarah. Addition hai system prompt me content jo model ko instruct karta hai ki uske paas kaunse tools available hain. Neeche ek example formatted data point hai — system prompt aur JSON format me available tools ke saath.

Example — movie tools

<system>
You are a function-calling AI model. You are provided with function signatures
within <functions></functions> XML tags. You may call one or more functions to
assist with the user query. Don't make assumptions about what values to plug into
functions.
</system>
<functions>
[
  {
     "name": "search_movies",
     "description": "Search for movies by title and return matching results with IDs.",
     "parameters": {
       "type": "object",
       "properties": {
         "query": {"type": "string", "description": "The search string for the movie title."}
       },
       "required": ["query"]
     }
  },
  {
     "name": "get_movie_details",
     "description": "Fetch detailed information about a movie including cast, runtime, and synopsis.",
     "parameters": {
       "type": "object",
       "properties": {
         "movie_id": {"type": "string", "description": "The unique identifier for the movie."}
       },
       "required": ["movie_id"]
     }
  },
  {
     "name": "get_showtimes",
     "description": "Get movie showtimes for a given location and date.",
     "parameters": {
       "type": "object",
       "properties": {
         "movie_id": {"type": "string", "description": "The unique identifier for the movie."},
         "zip_code": {"type": "string", "description": "ZIP code for theater location."},
         "date": {"type": "string", "description": "Date for showtimes in YYYY-MM-DD format."}
       },
       "required": ["movie_id", "zip_code"]
     }
  }
]
</functions>
<user>
...
</user>

Language model generate karte time, upar wale example ko follow karke, tokens search_movies("Star Wars") generate karega Star Wars search karne ke liye. Ye aksar special formatting tokens ke andar encode hota hai, aur phir sequence me insert kiye gaye next tokens me tool outputs honge. Isse models simple standalone models se zyada challenging tasks accomplish karna seekh sakte hain.

Code execution — reasoning tokens ke andar

Tool use ka ek popular form code-execution hai, jo model ko complex logic ya mathematics problems ke precise answers dene deta hai. Example ke liye, code-execution reasoning model ke thinking tokens ke dauraan ho sakta hai. Function calling ki tarah, pehle execute karne wale code ke liye tags hote hain (model se generate kiye gaye) aur phir output ke liye alag tag.

Prompt: What is the 50th Fibonacci number? (Use the standard F_0=0, F_1=1 indexing.)
Thinking: Okay, I will compute the 50-th Fibonacci number with a simple loop,
then return the result.
<code>
def fib(n):
    a, b = 0, 1
    for _ in range(n):
        a, b = b, a + b
    return a
fib(50)
</code>
<output>
12586269025
</output>
Response: The 50-th Fibonacci number is 12 586 269 025.

Orchestration loop — under the hood kya hota hai

Language model tool inputs aur outputs ko standard autoregressively generated tokens ke saath interleave kar raha hai. Orchestration loop jo ye possible banata hai, kuch aisa dikhta hai:

messages = [...]
while True:
    response = model(messages, tools=tools)
    if not response.tool_calls:
        return response.text
    for call in response.tool_calls:
         result = execute_tool(call.name, call.args)
         messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": result})

Tool use ke liye training model ko is alag token flow ke saath predictably behave karna sikhane ke baare me hai — kab tool call emit karni hai, arguments ko sahi format kaise karna hai, aur results ko apne response me kaise incorporate karna hai. Open models ko variety of tools ke saath kaam karne ke liye train karna padta hai jo users off the shelf connect kar sakte hain.

Messages format — ek aur example

Overall structure tool-use ke liye same hai, lekin model ke turns tool calls se delimited subsections me split hote hain. Ek example: system message me function signatures aur live_giveaways_by_type function (GamerPower API se live giveaways retrieve karne ke liye, type parameter ke saath — game, loot, ya beta; default "game"); user message: "Where can I find live giveaways for beta access and games?"; assistant message: function_calls: live_giveaways_by_type(type='beta'), live_giveaways_by_type(type='game') — ek hi turn me do tool calls.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 13
← PreviousTool Use & Function Calling — models tools kaise use karte hainNext →Multi-step tool reasoning aur Model Context Protocol (MCP)
13.3Chapter 13 — Tool Use & Function Calling

Multi-step tool reasoning aur Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Multi-step tool use tab exciting research area bana jab reasoning models take off hue aur tool-use capabilities solidify hui. Iske saath Model Context Protocol (MCP) ek open standard ban gaya language models ko external data sources se connect karne ke liye.

Multi-step tool reasoning (13.2)

Ek leading lab ka o3 model multi-step tool-use ko language models ke saath integrate karne me substantial step-change represent karta hai. Ye behavior community me bahut pehle ke research trends se related hai. Example: ReAct ne showcase kiya kaise reasoning traces aur task-specific actions ek model generation me interleaved tareeke se generate kiye jaa sakte hain:

"We explore the use of LLMs to generate both reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner, allowing for greater synergy between the two: reasoning traces help the model induce, track, and update action plans as well as handle exceptions, while actions allow it to interface with and gather additional information from external sources such as knowledge bases or environments."

Tool-use capabilities ke solidify hone aur reasoning models ke take-off ke saath, multi-turn tool-use ek exciting research area me badh gaya hai.

Model Context Protocol — MCP (13.3)

Model Context Protocol (MCP) ek open standard hai language models ko external data sources aur information systems se connect karne ke liye. Data layer par, MCP JSON-RPC use karta hai — ye protocol ka transport aur message format hai. MCP ke aane se tools ko connect karna ek common formatting me standardize hua, bajay har tool ke liye alag integration likhne ke.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 13
← PreviousGeneration me tool calls interweave karna — format aur orchestrationNext →Tool use ki implementation considerations
13.4Chapter 13 — Tool Use & Function Calling

Tool use ki implementation considerations

Tool use ko production me implement karte time kuch lower-level considerations aate hain — tokenization aur message formats se lekar context consumption tak. Ye section unhe cover karta hai.

Tokenization aur message format details

Tool calls ek common messages format me aksar chat templates ke through tokenization se guzarti hain (code jo messages ko model ko bheje jaane wale format ko control karta hai) — structured JSON representations ko raw token streams me convert karte hue. Ye process model architectures ke across vary karti hai — kuch special tokens use karte hain tool calls demarcate karne ke liye, jabki doosre token stream ke andar hi structured formatting maintain karte hain. Chat template playgrounds ek interactive environment provide karte hain explore karne ke liye ki alag models message formats ko token streams me kaise convert karte hain.

Reasoning token continuity

Jaise reasoning models emerge hue hain, unki separate token stream — answer se pehle "reasoning" — ke saath tool-use loop me alag implementations exist karti hain ki unhe kaise handle kiya jaaye. Kuch models ek hi turn ke andar multiple tool invocations ke across reasoning tokens preserve karte hain, context maintain karte hue. Halanki, ye tokens typically turns ke beech erase kar diye jaate hain serving cost minimize karne ke liye (lekin hamesha nahi — ye ek design decision hai).

API formatting across providers (July 2025 tak)

Alag providers conceptually similar lekin technically distinct formats use karte hain. Ek leading provider tool_calls arrays use karta hai unique IDs ke saath, doosra detailed input_schema specifications use karta hai <thinking> tags ke saath, aur teesra function calling modes offer karta hai (AUTO/ANY/NONE). Jab in models ko API ke through use karte ho, to available tools JSON format me define kiye jaate hain aur phir model response me tool outputs standard "tokens generated" se alag field me store hote hain. Ek aur example: open-source vLLM inference codebase extensive parsing logic implement karta hai multiple tool calling modes aur model-specific parsers support karte hue — lower-level implementation considerations me insights deta hai.

Schema conformance aur constrained decoding

Production systems aksar valid JSON aur correct argument types enforce karte hain constrained decoding ya "strict mode" options use karke — malformed outputs se retries kam karte hue. Kuch closed model providers additional post-training karte hain specifically structured JSON output ko reliable banane ke liye, jahan open models ke liye ye ek inference flag ke roop me handle hota hai inference systems me.

Tool output context consumption

Tool outputs model ki context window ko jaldi consume kar sakte hain — khaas taur par search ya retrieval tools ke saath jo bahut se results return karte hain. Systems ko decide karna padta hai ki tool outputs ko kaise truncate, summarize, ya paginate kiya jaaye taaki context manageable rahe aur woh information preserve rahe jo model ko continue karne ke liye chahiye.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 13
← PreviousMulti-step tool reasoning aur Model Context Protocol (MCP)Next →Tool-use training data, objectives, aur evaluation
13.5Chapter 13 — Tool Use & Function Calling

Tool-use training data, objectives, aur evaluation

Post-training se tie karte hue: tool-use training data kahan se aata hai, aur kaunse objectives use hote hain? Human-written tool traces collect karna expensive hai, to zyada tar modern tool-use corpora synthetic ya bootstrapped hain. Evaluation multiple dimensions me hoti hai.

Training data kahan se aata hai

Human-written tool traces collect karna expensive hai, to zyada tar modern tool-use corpora synthetic ya bootstrapped hain — Toolformer-style self-labeling ya ToolBench jaise large-scale generation. Training objectives:

  • Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on tool trajectories: basic formatting aur tool selection sikhata hai. Ye behavior bootstrap karta hai aur aksar skill ki foundation establish karne ke liye kaafi hota hai.
  • Preference optimization (jaise DPO) over trajectories: decisions improve kar sakta hai ki kab tool call karna hai vs seedha answer dena hai.
  • RL with environment feedback: multi-step tool use wale agentic tasks ke liye natural objective — model seekhta hai ki uske tool-augmented actions ne problem asal me solve kiya ya nahi (task success, constraint satisfaction).

Evaluation — multiple dimensions

Tool-use models evaluate karne me multiple dimensions involve hain: tool name aur argument correctness ke liye exact-match metrics, schema validity, aur simulated environments me end-to-end task completion. Trials ke across reliability bhi matter karti hai — τ-bench ne pass^k metric introduce kiya (pass@k se distinct) jo measure karta hai ki agent consistently succeed karta hai ya occasionally.

  • ToolLLM aur ToolBench dataset: 16,000+ real-world APIs ke across tool use train aur evaluate karne ka large-scale framework.
  • Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL): function calling accuracy par models compare karne ka popular benchmark.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 13
