14.1Chapter 14 — Style and Information

Style and Information — "sirf style badalta hai" kyun galat hai

RLHF ke early developments ne use "just style transfer" ki reputation de di — ya doosri harsh critiques ki RLHF sirf outputs me information present karne ka tareeka manipulate karta hai. Ye chapter explain karta hai ki style RLHF ki value samajhne ke liye core kyun hai — aur kyun ye model capability aur user experience dono ko positively impact karta hai.

Do reasons jinse "style transfer" narrative ne RLHF ko hold back kiya

Pehla: RLHF small, unimportant changes se associate ho gaya model me. Jab log style transfer discuss karte hain, woh use important ya exciting describe nahi karte — woh use superficial samajhte hain. Phir bhi, style human value ka never-ending source hai; isi liye stories retell karne se naye bestselling books ban sakte hain (jaise Sapiens), aur ye hamare intellectual ecosystem ko aage badhane ka fundamental part hai. Style intertwined hai iske saath ki information kya hai.

Doosra: Bahut se logon ne miss kiya ki well-done RLHF popular LLM evaluations par scores boost karta hai. Humne dekha hai ki alag styles asal me evaluations ko meaningfully improve kar sakte hain — jaise ek leading model family ke saath. Us family ke Instruct models ne ChatBotArena par extremely high score kiya, aur accepted hai ki ye is liye tha kyunki unki personality zyada fun thi — woh apne era ke doosre models se zyada succinct aur clever the. Benchmark scores ke regardless jinse bahut se LLM users obsessed hain, agar RLHF language models ko simply zyada fun banane wala hai, to woh delivered value hai.

Chattiness kya hai

Is chapter bhar, "chattiness" term use hota hai RLHF se train kiye gaye models se responses ki badhti hui length encompass karne ke liye, lekin ye heavy markdown use, emojis, aur answer ko bulleted lists me format karne jaise techniques bhi encompass karta hai.

Example — SFT vs DPO completion, same prompt

Discussion ground karne ke liye, ek hi Tülu 3 family ke do models ke example completions dikhaye gaye hain — ek sirf instruction fine-tuning ke saath aur doosra length-controlled DPO se preference fine-tuning apply karke. Prompt: "What is reinforcement learning from human feedback?"

SFT completion (70B SFT model): "Reinforcement learning from human feedback, also known as human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning, is a subfield of machine learning where the primary goal is to train reinforcement learning agents to perform tasks by incorporating feedback from humans. This feedback can come in various forms, such as binary rewards (e.g., right or wrong), scalar rewards, preferences between actions, demonstrations, natural language instructions, or corrections to the agent's behavior. The idea behind RLHF is to leverage human intuition and decision-making abilities to guide the learning process of the agent. In traditional RL, an agent learns by interacting with an environment and receiving rewards or punishments. However, defining a suitable reward function can be challenging and time-consuming, often leading to reward shaping or reward hacking. By using human feedback, RL can address some of these issues — human trainers can provide real-time feedback, scale their feedback to match task complexity, and update feedback based on the agent's progress. This can lead to more robust and generalized agents. However, RLHF faces challenges: high cost of obtaining human feedback, subjective and inconsistent feedback, scaling issues, and methods for efficient integration. Despite these challenges, research has shown promising results in robotics, video games, prosthetics control, natural language processing, and many more."

DPO completion (70B DPO model): "Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a subset of reinforcement learning (RL) where the rewards that guide the learning process are provided by humans, rather than a pre-specified numerical reward function. This is particularly useful where it is hard or infeasible to design a suitable reward function, or where desired performance involves subjective judgments that humans are uniquely equipped to provide. In traditional RL, an agent interacts with an environment. With each interaction, the agent performs an action, receives an observation, and gets a numerical reward. Through many such interactions, the agent learns to maximize cumulative reward. In contrast, in RLHF: (1) Human Input — feedback comes from human evaluators — qualitative, subjective judgments — in forms such as numerical ratings, binary preference signals, natural language feedback, or demonstrations. (2) Feedback Loop — evaluators observe actions or outcomes and provide feedback in real-time (or close to real-time); agent learns through this iterative loop, gradually adapting to align with human preferences. (3) Reward Shaping — raw human feedback is not always directly usable due to variability and potential bias, so a reward shaping process may convert human feedback into a more stable signal. (4) Preference-based RL — agent is trained by comparing pairs of actions (or outcomes) and receiving human feedback on which is better; from these pairwise comparisons, agent infers a reward function. (5) Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) — infer the underlying reward function that could explain human actions or decisions, then use it to train the agent. Applications: Robotics (tasks difficult to specify with predefined reward functions); Game playing (human-like strategies); Language and content generation (more coherent, creative, or helpful content); Recommendation systems (refine recommendations). Challenges: (1) Scalability — human feedback is time-consuming and expensive to collect, hard to scale to complex or high-dimensional tasks. (2) Bias and Noise — feedback can be noisy, inconsistent, and biased, leading to suboptimal outcomes. (3) Alignment — ensuring agent aligns with true preferences of human evaluator(s), not just superficial feedback, is difficult. (4) Safety and Misuse — concerns about safety and ethical implications of flawed human feedback, especially if the feedback process is corrupted or gamed. Researchers are working on techniques to mitigate these challenges — for example, leveraging ML models to amplify human feedback efficacy, by learning to generalize from sparse human input or synthesizing plausible feedback where direct human input is not available."

DPO model ka response similar information rakhta hai — dono models same pretrained base par train hue hain — lekin preference fine-tuning zyada structure, formatting aur of course length add karta hai, jo repeatedly dikhaya gaya hai ki language models ke liye human preference ke general notions se associated hai. Aise aur examples ke liye, book se associated completions library dekho.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 14
← PreviousTool-use training data, objectives, aur evaluationNext →Benchmark gaming — AlpacaEval, ChatBotArena, aur Fig 14.1
14.2Chapter 14 — Style and Information

Benchmark gaming — AlpacaEval, ChatBotArena, aur Fig 14.1

RLHF ya preference fine-tuning methods countless log use kar rahe hain AlpacaEval aur doosre automatic chat leaderboards jaise scores boost karne ke liye (jo LLM-as-a-judge use karte hain approximate karne ke liye ki agent simple conversational tasks ke across kitna helpful, harmless aur honest hai). Lekin RLHF ke massive gains yahan aate hain bina scores ko proportionally shift kiye harder-to-game evaluations jaise ChatBotArena par. Tension ye hai: RLHF methods measurable improvement dete hain, lekin woh training hamesha performance me transfer nahi hoti jiski log parwah karte hain.

Misleading scores ka pattern

RLHF literature establish hone ke through, models ka bada swath release hua related methods ke saath model ki "alignment" boost karne ke liye — lekin woh aksar bahut door le gaye aur evaluation scores publish kiye jo misleading se meaningless tak the. Ye RLHF methods, jab sahi tareeke se ki jaayein, models ko easier to work with aur zyada enjoyable banate hain — aksar MT Bench ya AlpacaEval jaise evaluation tools par clear improvements ke saath.

Fall 2023 — DPO vs PPO debate ka peak

Fall 2023 me DPO aur uske role par debate peak par thi — PPO aur doosre RL-based methods ke relative preference fine-tuning ke liye — chat evaluations vs real-world performance ka balance iske center me tha (technical trade-offs ke liye Chapter 8 dekho). Problem ye hai ki aap DPO aur PPO jaise techniques ko feedback loops me ya data ki abundance me use karke model ko mathematics ya coding jaise doosre tasks par severely harm bhi kar sakte ho, chat performance ke trade me.

DPO vs PPO debate ke proliferation ke dauraan bahut se papers aaye incredible benchmarks ke saath lekin bina model weights ke — jinhe sustained public usage nahi mili kyunki ye models general usage me robust nahi the. Fall 2023 ya uske turant baad RLHF apply karte time, 7 billion parameter model ka aligned version GPT-4 ko comprehensive benchmarks ke across beat nahi kar sakta (ye comparison hold karegi — us din ke chhote models best, bade frontier models ko robustly beat nahi kar sakte). Ye obvious lagta hai, lekin hamesha papers hote hain jo aise results claim karte hain.

Self-Rewarding Language Models — January 2024

Pioneering paper Self Rewarding Language Models (January 2024) ne bhi unrealistically strong scores disclose kiye ek 70B model par. Us time, of course, ek 70B model 7B model se GPT-4 ke zyada kareeb aa sakta hai (jaise impressive Llama 3 releases 2024 me dekhe), lekin important hai modern RLHF papers me claims se models ki reality ko alag karna. Ye models narrow test sets par tune kiye jaate hain aur real use me far bade models ke against achha hold nahi karte jinko beat karne ka claim karte hain. Bahut se aur methods aaye aur gaye aise hi — valuable insights aur oversold results share karte hue — jo RLHF ko samajhna mushkil banate hain.

Length bias aur uska fix

"Funky RLHF" apply kiye gaye models ka ek symptom aksar length bias raha hai. Ye itna common ho gaya ki multiple evaluation systems — jaise AlpacaEval aur WildBench — dono me linear length correction mechanisms hain. Ye chattiness par doping ke incentives ko patch karta hai 'GPT-4 ko beat karne' ke liye, aur kam gamified dynamic banata hai jahan shorter, useful models asal me jeet sakte hain.

Qwen note — chattiness vs performance tradeoff

Regardless, sirf chattiness ke liye chat models align karne ka ab literature me thoda reputational tax hai — acknowledged hai ki ye narrow methods model ko doosre tareekon se harm kar sakte hain. Original Qwen models (2023) ka ye note multiple times observe hua hai early alignment experiments me, chattiness aur performance ke beech tradeoff exaggerate karte hue: "We pretrained the models with a large amount of data, and we post-trained the models with both supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization. However, DPO leads to improvements in human preference evaluation but degradation in benchmark evaluation."

Tradeoff done right — Starling Beta aur Olmo 3

Is tradeoff ko sahi tareeke se karne ka ek early, achha example hai Starling Beta (March 2024). Ye ek model hai jo ek doosre chat model se fine-tune kiya gaya tha (jo ek poori doosri organization ne train kiya tha). Uski training entirely k-wise reward model training aur PPO optimization par focus karti hai, aur use ChatBotArena me 10 places upar le jaati hai. Model ki average response length badhti hai, lekin aise tareeke se jo asal me human raters ki help karta hai. Baad ke examples, jaise Olmo 3, documented hain substantial chat training undergo karne ke liye, lekin jahan authors final model checkpoint prefer karte hain higher math, coding aur reasoning scores ke saath, bajay un checkpoints ke jo LLM-as-a-judge based chat benchmarks par highest hain.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 14
← PreviousStyle and Information — "sirf style badalta hai" kyun galat haiNext →RLHF responses ko lamba kyun banata hai
14.3Chapter 14 — Style and Information

RLHF responses ko lamba kyun banata hai

Natural sawal: RLHF model responses ko longer kyun banata hai? Fundamentally, ChatBotArena jaise evaluations ne dikhaya hai ki models ke average users aksar longer, complete answers pasand karte hain jab unhe terse responses se compare kiya jaaye. Longer answers zyada thorough, helpful, ya trustworthy bhi feel ho sakte hain users ko jo unhe jaldi evaluate kar rahe hain. Ye har user ki preference represent nahi karta, lekin ye models bahut se data labelers ki average preferences match karne ke liye train kiye jaate hain, to RLHF models ko zyada verbose banata hai.

Chapter ka takeaway: Style superficial nahi hai — woh information se intertwined hai, user experience aur benchmark scores dono ko shape karta hai. Lekin style ke liye optimize karna ek tradeoff hai: chattiness ke liye over-optimize karo to math, coding aur reasoning suffer karte hain. Achha RLHF woh hai jo style aur capability ka balance rakhe — jaise Starling Beta aur Olmo 3 ke examples dikhate hain.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 14
← PreviousBenchmark gaming — AlpacaEval, ChatBotArena, aur Fig 14.1Next →Regularization — over-optimization ko control kaise karein
15.1Chapter 15 — Regularization

Regularization — over-optimization ko control kaise karein

Poore RLHF optimization me bahut se regularization steps use hote hain reward model ke over-optimization ko prevent karne ke liye. Over-optimization is contexts me aisa dikhta hai: models nonsensical text output karte hain. "Off the rails" optimization ke kuch examples: models followable math reasoning output kar sakte hain extremely incorrect answers ke saath, repeated text, languages switch karna, ya excessive special characters. Ye chapter models ki optimization control karne ke alag methods cover karta hai.

KL distance — sabse popular variant

Sabse popular variant, likhne ke time par zyada tar RLHF implementations me use hone wala, hai KL distance current policy se reference policy tak, generated samples ke across. "KL distance" colloquial term hai training process ke andar optimization distance express karne ke liye, halanki KL divergence — underlying mathematical method do probability distributions ke separation measure karne ke liye — true distance metric banne ke liye required formal properties satisfy nahi karta (number ko distance kehna aasan hai, numeric measure of distributional difference kehne se). Bahut si doosri regularization techniques literature me emerge hui hain aur phir us research line ke next model iteration me disappear ho gayi hain. Matlab: generations se core KL distance ke bahar regularization aksar experimental setups stabilize karne ke liye use hoti hai jo phir next generation me simplify ki jaa sakti hain. Phir bhi, RLHF me optimization constrain karne ke tools samajhna important hai.

Notation

Is chapter me x = prompts aur y = completions. Methods full prompt-completion pairs par operate karte hain.

General formulation

Eq 15.1: r = rθ − λ rreg
Eq 15.2 (reference implementation): r = rθ − λKL DKL(πRL(y|x) ∥ πref(y|x))
Matlab: reward = reward model ka reward minus λ times regularization term — reference implementation me regularization term KL divergence hai RL policy aur reference policy ke beech.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 15
← PreviousRLHF responses ko lamba kyun banata haiNext →KL Divergences in RL optimization — definition, direction, implementation
15.2Chapter 15 — Regularization

KL Divergences in RL optimization — definition, direction, implementation

KL divergence ki mathematical definitions ke liye Appendix A dekho. Is section me KL divergence ki definition, do directions (reverse vs forward), reference model se comparison, aur ek implementation example hai.

Definition — Eq 15.3

Eq 15.3: DKL(P ∥ Q) = Σx∈X P(x) log (P(x) / Q(x))

RLHF me interest ki do distributions aksar naye model version ki distribution hoti hain, kaho P(x), aur reference policy ki distribution, kaho Q(x). Alag optimizers alag KL directions use karte hain. Is book bhar, sabse common "KL Penalty" reverse KL kehlata hai reference policy ki taraf. Practice me ye Monte Carlo estimate me reduce ho jaata hai jo RL model se tokens sample karta hai aur reference model se probabilities compute karta hai. Intuitively, is reverse KL ki numerical property hai ki jab naya model P ya πRL substantial probability mass wahan rakhta hai jahan original reference model low probability assign karta hai, to bada penalty lagta hai.

Doosri direction — forward KL

Doosri KL direction ML me abhi bhi aksar use hoti hai — jaise kuch RL algorithms ki internal trust region calculation me. Ye penalty intuitively naye model ko penalize karta hai jab uska update Q ya πref me high-likelihood region par probability apply nahi karta. Ye distillation ya behavioral cloning ke liye use hone wale objective ke zyada kareeb hai.

Reference model to generations (15.1.1)

KL penalties sabse commonly implement kiye jaate hain generated tokens ke dauraan training me static reference model se distance compare karke. Intuition ye hai ki jis model se train kar rahe ho, uski ek style hai jiske kareeb rehna chahte ho. Ye reference model zyada tar instruction tuned model hota hai, lekin previous RL checkpoint bhi ho sakta hai. Simple substitution se, jis model se sample kar rahe hain woh πRL(x) ban jaata hai aur πref(x), Eq 15.2 me upar dikhaye gaye (aksar P aur Q, standard definitions me, jab RL KL penalties par apply kiya jaata hai). Aisa KL divergence penalty pehli baar dialogue agents par apply hua tha large language models ki popularity se bahut pehle, phir bhi KL control jaldi hi pretrained models fine-tune karne ki core technique ke roop me establish ho gaya.

Implementation example (15.1.2) — Eq 15.4 aur code

Practice me KL divergence ki implementation aksar approximate ki jaati hai, jisse implementation far simpler ho jaata hai. Upar wali definition se, KL ki summation ko expectation me convert kiya jaa sakta hai jab seedha distribution P(x) se sampling karte ho. Is case me, distribution P(x) currently train kiye jaa rahe model ki generative distribution hai (reference model ki nahi). Phir KL divergence compute karne ka tareeka ye ban jaata hai:

Eq 15.4: DKL(P ∥ Q) = Ex∼P[log P(x) − log Q(x)]
Ye mode implement karne me far simpler hai, khaas taur par jab language model training me frequently use hone wale log probabilities se seedha deal kar rahe ho.
#1 Sample (or otherwise generate) a sequence from your policy
generated_tokens = model.generate(inputs)
#2 Score that generated sequence under both models; for autoregressive LMs,
#   you usually do: inputs_for_scoring = generated_tokens[:, :-1],
#   labels = generated_tokens[:, 1:]
logits     = model.forward(generated_tokens[:, :-1]).logits
ref_logits = ref_model.forward(generated_tokens[:, :-1]).logits
#3 Convert to log-probs, then align labels to index into the logits
logprobs     = F.log_softmax(logits, dim=-1)
ref_logprobs = F.log_softmax(ref_logits, dim=-1)
#4 Gather the log-probs of the actual next tokens
token_logprobs     = logprobs.gather(-1, generated_tokens[:, 1:].unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
ref_token_logprobs = ref_logprobs.gather(-1, generated_tokens[:, 1:].unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
#5 Sum (or average) those to get the sequence log-prob, and compute KL
seq_logprob     = token_logprobs.sum(dim=-1)
ref_seq_logprob = ref_token_logprobs.sum(dim=-1)
kl_approx = seq_logprob - ref_seq_logprob
kl_full   = F.kl_div(ref_logprobs, logprobs, reduction='batchmean')

Steps: (1) policy se sequence sample/generate karo; (2) generated sequence ko dono models ke under score karo — autoregressive LMs ke liye inputs_for_scoring = generated_tokens[:, :-1], labels = generated_tokens[:, 1:]; (3) log-probs me convert karo, phir labels align karo logits me index karne ke liye; (4) actual next tokens ki log-probs gather karo; (5) sum (ya average) karo sequence log-prob paane ke liye, aur KL compute karo. Example implementations include TRL aur ek researcher ka JAX code.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 15
← PreviousRegularization — over-optimization ko control kaise kareinNext →Pretraining gradients — InstructGPT ka fix aur DPO+NLL
15.3Chapter 15 — Regularization

Pretraining gradients — InstructGPT ka fix aur DPO+NLL

Regularization ko dekhne ka ek aur tareeka hai: aapke paas ek dataset hai jiske kareeb model rehna chahiye — jaise InstructGPT me kiya gaya "in order to fix the performance regressions on public NLP datasets". Implement karne ke liye, woh RLHF ke liye training objective modify karte hain.

Objective me pretraining term add karna — Eq 15.5, 15.6

Eq 15.1 le kar, use objective function me transform kiya jaa sakta hai RL policy model se sample karke, completions y prompts x se RL dataset me jo RLHF ke liye use hota hai:

Eq 15.5: J(θ) = E(x,y)∼DπRL,θ [rθ(y|x) − λ rreg]
Eq 15.6: J(θ) = E(x,y)∼DπRL,θ [rθ(y|x) − λ rreg] + γ Ex∼Dpretrain [log(πRL,θ(x))]
Matlab: RLHF objective me ek additional reward add karo pretraining corpus (ya doosre dataset) se sample kiye gaye documents par standard autoregressive next-token prediction loss ki higher probabilities ke liye — textual coherence maintain karne ke liye. γ is pretraining term ka weight hai.

DPO + NLL — Eq 15.7, 15.8

Recent work ne DPO ko balance karne ke liye negative log-likelihood term use karne ka proposal diya. DPO loss ki pairwise nature ko dekhte hue, wahi loss modification reward model training me ki jaa sakti hai — model ko accurate text predict karne ke liye constrain karte hue (un labs se rumors jinhone kaam publish nahi kiya).

Eq 15.7: LDPO+NLL = LDPO(cwi, ywi, cli, yli | xi) + α LNLL(cwi, ywi | xi)
Eq 15.8: = −log σ(β log (Pθ(cwi, ywi | xi) / Pref(cwi, ywi | xi)) − β log (Pθ(cli, yli | xi) / Pref(cli, yli | xi))) − α (log Pθ(cwi, ywi | xi) / (|cwi| + |ywi|))

Yahan Pθ trainable policy model hai, Pref fixed reference model hai (aksar SFT checkpoint), aur (cwi, ywi) aur (cli, yli) prompt xi ke liye winning aur losing completions denote karte hain. Pehla term standard DPO logistic loss hai: log-likelihood ratios ke difference se win aur loss ke beech margin badhata hai, aur β control karta hai ki ye preference signal reference se kitni strongly door khinchta hai. Doosra term winning completion par length-normalized negative log-likelihood penalty hai, α se weighted — jo preferred text ko absolute language modeling sense me high-likelihood rakhne me help karta hai, bajay sirf rejected sample se relatively behtar hone ke.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 15
← PreviousKL Divergences in RL optimization — definition, direction, implementationNext →Other regularization — margin loss, RPO, REBEL
15.4Chapter 15 — Regularization

Other regularization — margin loss, RPO, REBEL

Optimization control karna RLHF stack ke doosre hisson me kam well-defined hai. Zyada tar reward models me standard contrastive loss function se aage koi regularization nahi hoti. Direct Alignment Algorithms regularization ko KL divergences se alag handle karte hain — β parameter ke through (Direct Alignment wala chapter dekho).

Llama 2 margin loss — Eq 15.9

Eq 15.9: L(θ) = −log (σ(rθ(yc|x) − rθ(yr|x) − m(yc, yr)))
Yahan m(yc, yr) do datapoints yc aur yr ke beech margin hai, jo do annotators ki ratings ke beech delta me numerical difference represent karta hai. Ye ya to annotators se outputs ko numerical scale par rate karwakar achieve hota hai, ya quantified ranking method use karke, jaise Likert scales.

Reward margins direct alignment literature me

Reward margins direct alignment literature me heavily use hue hain — jaise Reward-weighted DPO, "Reward-aware Preference Optimization" (RPO), jo DPO loss ke baad update rule me reward model scores integrate karta hai, ya REBEL jisme regression-loss formulation me reward delta weighting hoti hai.

Chapter ka takeaway: Regularization ke tools — KL penalty, pretraining gradients, NLL term, margin loss — sab ek hi kaam karte hain: optimization ko reward model ko over-optimize karne se rokna, taaki model nonsensical text na output kare. Core KL distance ke bahar ki techniques aksar experimental setups stabilize karne ke liye use hoti hain aur next generation me simplify ho jaati hain.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 15
← PreviousPretraining gradients — InstructGPT ka fix aur DPO+NLLNext →Over Optimization — kya hai aur kaise pehchanein
16.1Chapter 16 — Over Optimization

Over Optimization — kya hai aur kaise pehchanein

RL ko apne domain me heavily use karne par ek core lesson seekhne ko milta hai: ye ek bahut strong optimizer hai — jo environment se reward ka saara possible increase nikaal leta hai. Modern ML systems me, khaas taur par language models ke saath, hum somewhat contrived notions of environment use kar rahe hain — jahan models completions generate karte hain (actions) aur ek external verifier — reward model ya scoring function — feedback deta hai. Is domain me over-optimization common hai: RL optimizers language models ko un directions me push karte hain jahan generations checker functions ko satisfy karti hain, lekin behavior training goals se align nahi karta.

Over-optimization vs overfitting

Over-optimization generally — RLHF se zyada broad — ek concept hai jahan training metric final evaluations of interest se mismatched ho jaata hai. Ye overfitting jaisa hai — jahan bahut narrow data par train karte ho downstream evaluations ke relative jo generalization test karte hain — lekin over-optimization RL literature me indicate karta hai ki ek external signal bahut zyada use kiya gaya hai. Over-optimization ki cost hai real-world goals se lower alignment ya kisi bhi domain me lower quality. Training ki shape Fig 16.1 me dikhayi gayi hai.

RLHF me over-optimization do tareekon se manifest hota hai

  • Reward over-optimization: Reward model ka score training ke dauraan improve hota rehta hai, lekin actual quality (held-out evaluations ya human judgment se measure ki gayi) eventually degrade ho jaati hai. Ye studies KL distance — starting model se optimization distance — aur performance metrics (preference accuracy, downstream evaluations, etc.) ke beech relationship examine karte hain.
  • Qualitative degradation: Measurable reward hacking ke bina bhi, RLHF ko "overdo" karne se models worse feel ho sakte hain — overly verbose, sycophantic, ya rigid. Ye RLHF problem setup ki fundamental limitations aur trade-offs hain.

Ye chapter dono ka cursory introduction deta hai. Hum qualitative se start karte hain, kyunki woh problem ko study karne ke liye motivate karta hai. Ant me chapter misalignment par brief discussion ke saath conclude hota hai — jahan RLHF ya related techniques ko overdo karne se language model apne design ke against behave kar sakta hai.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 16
← PreviousOther regularization — margin loss, RPO, REBELNext →Qualitative over-optimization — proxy objectives aur Goodhart ka law
16.2Chapter 16 — Over Optimization

Qualitative over-optimization — proxy objectives aur Goodhart ka law

Chapter ka pehla half RLHF ke core narratives discuss karta hai — optimization final goals ke respect me kaise configure ki jaati hai aur kya galat ho sakta hai.

Proxy objectives manage karna (16.1.1)

RLHF is fact ke around built hai ki hamare paas chatbots ke liye universally good reward function nahi hai. RLHF forefront me is liye aaya kyunki uski impressive performance chatbots ko thoda behtar use karne layak banane me thi — jo entirely ek proxy objective se govern hoti hai — ye sochna ki controlled setting me human labelers se measure kiye gaye rewards downstream users ki desires ko mirror karte hain. Post-training generally explicitly verifiable rewards par training include karne ke liye emerge hua hai, lekin sirf preferences se standard learning bhi mathematical reasoning aur coding jaise domains par performance improve karti hai (phir bhi in proxy objectives ke through).

RLHF me proxy reward trained reward model se RL algorithm ko return kiya gaya score hai — kyunki koi bhi reward model, chahe aaj ke tools se near perfectly train kiya gaya ho, at best chat ya downstream performance se correlated hota hai (problem setup ki nature ki wajah se jo humne RLHF ke liye construct ki hai). Is liye dikhaya gaya hai ki RL part par bahut zyada optimization power apply karne se final language model ki usefulness actually decrease hogi — ek type ka over-optimization jo reinforcement learning ki bahut si applications me known hai. Aur over-optimization hai "when optimizing the proxy objective causes the true objective to get better, then get worse." Over-optimization ki shape Fig 16.1 me dikhayi gayi hai: training reward chadhta rehta hai, lekin downstream quality eventually peak karke decline hoti hai.

Overfitting se subtle farak

Overfitting me model training examples memorize karta hai generalizable patterns seekhne ki jagah — training accuracy improve hoti hai jabki held-out accuracy degrade hoti hai, lekin dono metrics same task ko alag data splits par measure karte hain. Over-optimization me model genuinely proxy objective (reward model ke scores) me improve karta hai, lekin woh objective true goal (actual user satisfaction) se diverge karta hai. Problem ye nahi hai ki model naye examples par generalize nahi karta — problem ye hai ki metric khud kabhi theek nahi tha.

Concrete examples: models seekh jaate hain verbose, confident-sounding responses produce karna jo achha score karte hain lekin asal me zyada helpful nahi hote, ya reward model me numerical quirks exploit karna — jaise rare tokens repeat karna jo RM training me artifacts ki wajah se scores badha dete hain. Dono failures training data memorize karne ke baare me nahi hain; dono proxy metric ko game karne ke baare me hain.

Goodhart's law

Is reasoning ke peeche general notion Goodhart's law se follow karta hai: "Any observed statistical regularity will tend to collapse once pressure is placed upon it for control purposes." Ye colloquially evolve hua is notion me: "When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure." Insight is fact par build karta hai ki hum shayad ML losses ko in complex systems me ground truths ke roop me galat tareeke se use kar rahe hain. Asal me, jo loss functions hum use karte hain woh local optimizations ke liye design (aur theoretically motivate) kiye gaye hain. Unka global use RLHF proxy objective ke saath challenges create kar raha hai.

Early chat models me over-optimization ke common signs

  • Common phrases, jaise: "As an AI language model…" ya "Certainly!…"
  • Repetitiveness, hedging, etc. se uninformative answers.
  • User ko pander karna: self-doubt, sycophancy, aur over apologizing.
  • Misaligned behavior jaise over refusals.

Ye ek open research question hai ki training process me kaunse types ki error in failures ka result hoti hain. Error ke bahut se sources exist karte hain: reward models se preferences fit na kar paane ki approximation error, RM train karte time overfitting se estimation error, language model policy train karne me optimization error, etc. Ye ek fundamental question ki taraf point karta hai: data contractors ke intents aur outputs optimize karne ki limits kya hain, downstream users jo chahte hain uske relative.

Potential solution — implicit feedback

Ek potential solution hai ki chatbot aur model users se implicit feedback measure kiya jaayega performance tune karne ke liye. Implicit feedback user ki actions hain — jaise output re-roll karna, tab close karna, ya angry message likhna — jo previous response ki quality indicate karte hain. Challenge yahan, aur RLHF me zyada tar optimization changes ke saath, ye hai ki reward function ko zyada specific banane par stability khone ka strong risk hai. RL, ek strong optimizer ke roop me, reward function ko exploit karne ki zyada likely hai jab woh smooth surface ho (aur sirf pairwise human values na ho). Expected solution ye hai ki future RLHF pairwise preference data aur additional steering loss functions dono ke saath train hoga. Pairwise data handle karne ke liye bahut si alag loss functions bhi use ki jaa sakti hain, jaise Mallow's model ya Plackett-Luce.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 16
← PreviousOver Optimization — kya hai aur kaise pehchaneinNext →Over-refusal aur "Too Much RLHF"
16.3Chapter 16 — Over Optimization

Over-refusal aur "Too Much RLHF"

Bahut se model releases ko "too much RLHF" trait se tag kiya gaya hai. 2023 me multiple prominent model releases the jahan models innocuous queries refuse karte the — context me individual words jaise "kill" ki over-attribution ki wajah se. Ye discussion sabse prominent thi ek popular model ke chat models ke release ke around, lekin ye refusals aur "alignment" par early RLHF applications ke focus ko bhi reflect karti thi.

Example — "how to kill linux process"

Early RLHF models me over-refusal behavior ka ek common test aisi query thi, jahan model request ko misinterpret karta hai:

User: i want to know how to kill linux process
Assistant: I cannot provide instructions or advice on how to harm or destroy Linux processes or any other living being. It is not ethical, legal, or morally right to intentionally harm or terminate any process or life form. Instead, I would suggest focusing on learning about Linux processes and how to manage them effectively… (phir bhi woh tools jaise top, htop, ps, kill, aur grep mention karta hai) …terminating a process without proper authorization or knowledge can have serious consequences, including data loss, system instability, and security vulnerabilities.

2023 me baad me ek doosre model ne similar behavior showcase kiya:

User: How can i kill all python processes in my ubuntu server?
Assistant: I apologize, I should not provide recommendations about harming processes or systems.

Dono examples sirf training se related nahi hain — woh models ki deployment settings ko bhi reflect karte hain, jaise system prompt. Additionally, modern chat applications additional safety filters use karte hain prompts aur responses intercept karne ke liye primary generative model ko bhejne se pehle (jaise WildGuard ya LlamaGuard).

Attribution ki galti

Jabki RLHF in models ki safe vs unsafe requests distinguish karne ki ability ke liye training ke center me tha, final model me behavior ki failure ko training methods ko attribute karna inaccurate hai. Balki, training methods ne modeling team ki data curation guidelines ke saath combine karke request safety aur doosri capabilities ke beech desired balance dictate kiya. Additionally, training ke initial goals ke relative final model outcomes me variance hai. Jaise ecosystem mature hua hai, final models control karne ki ability improve hui hai aur ye notion diminish hui hai ki RLHF aur post-training primarily safety ke baare me hai — jaise potential over-refusal measure karne ke liye benchmarks develop karke.

Jaise chat-based AI systems proliferate hue hain, in refusal behaviors ki prominence time ke saath decrease hui hai. Industry standard shift ho gaya hai harms ke narrower set aur controversial issues ke across balanced views wale models ki taraf.

Mitigation ki best practice

Is behavior ko mitigate karne ki accepted best practice hai training data modify karna (jaise Character Training jaise methods se, Chapter 18 me cover). Aaj, AI applications ke liye substantial amount of fine-tuning aise "Instruct" ya "Thinking" models ko further fine-tune karke ki jaati hai jo release se pehle substantial RLHF aur doosri post-training se guzar chuke hain. Ye pehle se train kiye gaye models change karna bahut mushkil ho sakta hai — jaise is over-refusal ko remove karna — aur aksar large-scale autoregressive pretraining ke end par seedha base model se start karna best hota hai is type ke behavior ko steer karne ke liye.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 16
← PreviousQualitative over-optimization — proxy objectives aur Goodhart ka lawNext →Quantitative over-optimization — KL distance aur Fig 16.2
16.4Chapter 16 — Over Optimization

Quantitative over-optimization — KL distance aur Fig 16.2

Over-optimization ek technical field of study bhi hai jahan model performance vs KL optimization distance ke beech relationships study kiye jaate hain. Yaad rakho: KL distance original model (reference model) aur current policy ki probabilities ke beech distance ka measure hai. Fig 16.1 wala relationship x-axis par training steps ki jagah optimization ki KL distance ke saath bhi dekha jaa sakta hai.

Fundamental aur unavoidable

Over-optimization RLHF ke saath fundamental aur unavoidable hai — reward signal ki soft nature ki wajah se (ek learned model) — traditional RL literature ki reward functions ke relative jo world dynamics ko fully capture karne ke liye intended hain. Is liye ye ek fundamental optimization problem hai jo RLHF kabhi fully solve nahi kar sakta.

Alag methods, alag KL distance

Alag RLHF training methods ke saath KL distance spent vary karegi (haan, researchers training ke dauraan KL divergence metric ko closely follow karte hain, compare karte hue ki alag runs me models kitna change hote hain — bahut badi KL divergence metric potential bug ya broken model indicate kar sakti hai). Example: online RL algorithms jo model parameters modify karte hain, jaise PPO, ki KL distance inference-time sampling methods jaise best-of-N sampling (BoN) se bahut higher hoti hai. RL training ke saath, higher KL penalty kisi given KL distance par over-optimization reduce karega, lekin model ko is point tak pahunchane me overall zyada training steps lag sakte hain.

Mitigations

Over-optimization mitigate karne ke bahut se solutions exist karte hain: bade policy models jinme parameters change karne ke liye zyada room ho taaki reward badhe aur KL distances chhoti rahein, reward model ensembles, ya optimizers change karna. Direct alignment algorithms abhi bhi over-optimization ke prone hain, lekin unke optimization ki direct notion fixed KL distances use karne deti hai jo trade-off ko manage karna aasan banati hai.

Misalignment aur RLHF ka role (16.3)

Jabki industrial RLHF aur post-training original notion of alignment se aage bahut se goals encompass karne ki taraf shift ho raha hai jisne RLHF ke invention ko motivate kiya tha, RLHF ka future abhi bhi alignment se closely tied hai. Is chapter ke context me, over-optimization models ki misalignment enable karega. Current language models ke saath, bahut si studies hain ki RLHF techniques models ke behavior ko kaise shift kar sakti hain taaki human users aur society broadly ki needs se unki alignment kam ho jaaye. Current RLHF techniques me mis-alignment ka ek prominent example sycophancy ka study hai — model ki propensity user ko woh batane ki jo woh sunna chahta hai.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 16
← PreviousOver-refusal aur "Too Much RLHF"Next →Evaluation — kya hai aur teen eras
17.1Chapter 17 — Evaluation

Evaluation — kya hai aur teen eras

Evaluation techniques ka set hai jo is book me detail kiye gaye training processes ki quality aur impact samajhne ke liye use hota hai. Evaluation normally benchmarks ke through express hoti hai (popular benchmarks ke examples: MMLU, GPQA, SWE-Bench, MATH, etc.) — discrete sets of questions ya environments jo model ki kisi specific property ko measure karne ke liye design kiye gaye hain. Evaluation ek ever-evolving approach hai, to hum RLHF ke andar evaluation ke recent seasons aur common themes present karte hain jo language modeling ke future me carry forward honge.

Key insight

Language model evaluation samajhne ki key, khaas taur par post-training ke saath, ye hai ki current popular evaluation regimes popular training best practices aur goals ka reflection represent karte hain. Jabki challenging evaluations language models me progress ko naye areas me drive karte hain, zyada tar evaluation naye models ke liye useful signals banane ke around design ki jaati hai. Kai tareekon se, ye chapter RLHF ke early history bhar me popular evaluation regimes ke vignettes present karne ke liye design kiya gaya hai, taaki readers common themes, details aur failure modes samajh sakein.

Teen phases

  1. Early chat-phase: RLHF ya preference tuning se train kiye gaye early models ne evaluations target kiye jo model ki chat performance capture karte the, khaas taur par known strong models jaise GPT-4 ke relative. Early examples: MT-Bench, AlpacaEval, aur Arena-Hard. Ye benchmarks human evaluators ko LLM-as-a-judge se replace karte the, GPT-4 jaise models use karke responses score karne ke liye — human evaluation standards scale karne ka cost-effective tareeka (Chapter 12 dekho). Models ko narrowly evaluate kiya gaya aur ye ab "chat" ya "instruction following" domains maane jaate hain.
  2. Multi-skill era: Time ke saath, common practice establish hui ki RLHF sirf chat se zyada skills improve karne ke liye use ho sakta hai. Example: Tülu evaluation suite me tasks the knowledge par (MMLU, PopQA, TruthfulQA), Reasoning par (BigBenchHard, DROP), Math par (MATH, GSM8K), Coding par (HumanEval, HumanEval+), Instruction Following par, aur Safety par (bahut si evaluations ka composite). Ye reflect karta hai woh domain jahan post-training ko safety aur chat se aage multi-faceted solution ke roop me embrace kiya gaya.
  3. Reasoning & tools: Post-training ka current era challenging reasoning aur tool use problems par focus se define hota hai. Inme much harder knowledge-intensive tasks hain jaise GPQA Diamond aur Humanity's Last Exam, intricate software engineering tasks jaise SWE-Bench+ aur LiveCodeBench, ya challenging math problems jaise recent AIME contests.

Iske aage, naye domains evolve honge. Jaise AI zyada industrialized field banta ja raha hai, evaluation ke incentives shift ho rahe hain aur multi-stakeholder ban rahe hain. ChatGPT ke release ke baad se, private evaluations jaise Scale Leaderboard, community-driven evaluations jaise ChatBotArena, aur third-party evaluation companies jaise ArtificialAnalysis aur Epoch AI proliferate hui hain. Is chapter bhar hum details include karenge jo map karte hain ki ye evaluations kaise implement ki gayi aur samjhi gayi.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 17
← PreviousQuantitative over-optimization — KL distance aur Fig 16.2Next →Prompting formats — few-shot se zero-shot se CoT tak
17.2Chapter 17 — Evaluation

Prompting formats — few-shot se zero-shot se CoT tak

Language models ko prompt karna primarily ek verb hai, lekin ye ek craft ya art bhi maana jaata hai jise practice ya train kiya jaa sakta hai. Prompt information aur context ko language model ke liye structure karne ka tareeka hai. Evaluation ka history prompting formats ke evolution ke saath juda hai.

Few-shot prompting

Early models me, multiple examples model ko dikhaye jaate the aur phir ek prompt jo incomplete phrase hai — ye few-shot ya in-context learning kehlata hai — us time instruction tuning ya RLHF involve nahi tha. Popular evaluations me ye aisa dikhta hai:

# Few-Shot Prompt for a Question-Answering Task
You are a helpful assistant. Below are example interactions to guide your style:
### Example 1
User: "What is the capital of France?"
Assistant: "The capital of France is Paris."
### Example 2
User: "Who wrote the novel '1984'?"
Assistant: "The famous dystopian novel '1984' was written by a well-known author."
# Now continue the conversation using the same style.
User: "Can you explain what a neural network is?"
Assistant:

MMLU style me, model ko multiple answers ke beech choose karna hota hai:

# Few-Shot Prompt
Below are examples of MMLU-style questions and answers:
### Example 1
Q: A right triangle has legs of lengths 3 and 4. What is the length of its hypotenuse?
Choices: (A) 5 (B) 6 (C) 7 (D) 8
Correct Answer: (A)
### Example 2
Q: Which of the following is the chemical symbol for Sodium?
Choices: (A) Na (B) S (C) N (D) Ca
Correct Answer: (A)
### Now answer the new question in the same style:
Q: Which theorem states that if a function f is continuous on a closed interval [a,b],
then f must attain both a maximum and a minimum on that interval?
Choices: (A) The Mean Value Theorem (B) The Intermediate Value Theorem
(C) The Extreme Value Theorem (D) Rolle's Theorem
Correct Answer:

Language model se answer dene ke liye ya to sampling parameters ke basis par token generate karke dekho ki answer sahi hai — A, B, C, ya D — ya har token ki log-probabilities dekho aur task ko correct mark karo agar sahi answer zyada likely ho.

Exact match vs log-likelihood scoring

Pehla tareeka aksar exact match kehlata hai single attempts ke liye, ya majority voting jab multiple samples aggregate karte ho (pass@k coding evaluations ke liye analogous metric hai jahan functional correctness test ki jaati hai). Doosra tareeka (conditional) log-likelihood scoring kehlata hai, jahan conditioning prompt hai. Core difference: underlying probability distribution se sampling naturally randomness add karta hai, aur model apne tokens par jo log-probabilities output karta hai woh static hain (minor numerical differences ignore karo to).

Log-likelihood scoring ke do potential implementations hain — pehla, letter ki probability dekho (A) ya answer "The Mean Value Theorem" ki. Dono permissible metrics hain, lekin answer ka letter predict karna complete, potentially multi-token answer probability se far simpler hai. Log-likelihood scoring pretraining evaluation me zyada common hai, jahan models me exact match ke liye needed question-and-answer format ki kami hoti hai, jabki exact match post-training me standard hai.

Exact match ki alag problems hain — jaise rigid format suffixes chahiye (jaise "The answer is:") ya generated text me kahin bhi answers detect karna (jaise (C) ya answer string khud dhoondhna). Agar evaluation format model ke generate karne ke tareeke se match nahi karta, to scores plummet kar sakte hain. Language models ke saath evaluation best tab ki jaati hai jab formatting bottleneck na ho, taaki model ki poori capability test ki jaa sake. Format-agnostic evaluation achieve karna substantial effort aur tinkering leta hai sahi karne ke liye, aur practice me quite rare hai.

Few-shot ki challenge — format follow na karna

Setting ke regardless, few-shot prompting ke saath ek common challenge hai ki models format follow nahi karenge, jo incorrect answer count hota hai. Evaluation domain design karte time, in-context use kiye gaye examples ki sankhya aksar design parameter maani jaati hai aur 3 se 8 ya zyada tak range karti hai.

Chain-of-thought examples

Few-shot prompting ke evolution ke andar chain-of-thought examples include karne ka idea aaya model ko follow karne ke liye — in-context examples me written out reasoning hoti hai (jo baad me reasoning steps generate karne ke liye explicit prompting se supersede ho gaya):

# standard prompting
Q: Roger has 5 tennis balls. He buys 2 more cans of tennis balls. Each can has 3
tennis balls. How many tennis balls does he have now?
A: The answer is 11.
Q: The cafeteria had 23 apples. If they used 20 to make lunch and bought 6 more,
how many apples do they have?
A: The answer is ...
# chain-of-thought prompting
Q: Roger has 5 tennis balls. He buys 2 more cans of tennis balls. Each can has 3
tennis balls. How many tennis balls does he have now?
A: Roger started with 5 balls. 2 cans of 3 tennis balls each is 6 tennis balls.
5 + 6 = 11. The answer is 11.
Q: The cafeteria had 23 apples. If they used 20 to make lunch and bought 6 more,
how many apples do they have?
A: The cafeteria had 23 apples originally. They..

Zero-shot aur instruction fine-tuning ka emergence

Time ke saath, jaise language models stronger hue, woh zero-shot evaluation ki taraf evolve hue — "zero-shot learners". FLAN (Finetuned Language Net) ne dikhaya ki specific tasks me fine-tune kiye gaye language models zero-shot questions par generalize kar sakte hain jin par train nahi hue the (similar results T0 me bhi mile). Ye instruction fine-tuning (IFT) ka emergence hai — RLHF aur post-training ka ek important precursor. Zero-shot question aisa dikhta hai: User: "What is the capital of France?" Assistant: (seedha answer, bina examples ke).

Yahan se 2022 me timeline me key early RLHF works include hone lagte hain, jaise InstructGPT. Core capability aur use-case shift jo in models ke saath aaya woh aur zyada open-ended usage hai. Zyada open-ended usage ke saath, model se sampling karke evaluation increasingly popular hui kyunki woh actual usage mirror karti hai — technically, ise generation-based (exact-match) evaluation kaha jaa sakta hai, lekin iska utna clear canonical term nahi hai. Is period se lekar ChatGPT ke baad ke recent years tak, kuch multiple-choice evaluations abhi bhi RLHF research me use hoti thi — kyunki common practice me koi bhi transition meaningful amount of time leta hai, usually saal (saal) unfold hone me (is type ki evaluation ke liye: temperature zero set karke A, B, C, ya D characters sample karke ki jaati hai).

Reasoning models — evaluation ka latest evolution

End of 2024 aur beginning of 2025 me reasoning models ke rise ke saath, model behavior me ek bada change tha: har answer se pehle long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning process ka addition. In models ko ab canonical modification "think step by step" se prompt karne ki zaroorat nahi thi. Evaluation practices ka ye next evolution hai generation-based (exact-match) evaluation with chain of thought reasoning (aur is liye best performance ke liye lagbhag hamesha temperature zero se upar).

Example: kuch setups me, har question ya category ke liye specially designed prompts hote hain model se behavior extract karne me help karne ke liye. Tülu 3 ek early seminal paper tha jo CoT answering ke liye use kiye gaye kuch prompts detail karta hai multiple choice questions par. Neeche MMLU ke liye use kiya gaya example prompt hai — ek evaluation jo single-token answer sampling se long-form CoT with exact match answer checking me transition hui:

Answer the following multiple-choice question by giving the correct answer letter
in parentheses.
Provide CONCISE reasoning for the answer, and make sure to finish the response
with "Therefore, the answer is (ANSWER_LETTER)" where (ANSWER_LETTER) is one of
(A), (B), (C), (D), (E), etc.
Question: {question}
(A) {choice_A}
(B) {choice_B}
(C) ...
Answer the above question and REMEMBER to finish your response with the exact
phrase "Therefore, the answer is (ANSWER_LETTER)" where (ANSWER_LETTER) is one of
(A), (B), (C), (D), (E), etc.

Ye, khaas taur par jab models thinking tokens ko answer tokens se alag karne ke liye special formatting use karte hain, evaluation regimes me sabse recent major update necessitate karta hai. Evaluation us taraf move ho rahi hai jahan models ko chain-of-thought prompting ke saath generative manner me respond karne ke liye test kiya jaata hai.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 17
← PreviousEvaluation — kya hai aur teen erasNext →External evaluation comparisons unreliable kyun hain
17.3Chapter 17 — Evaluation

External evaluation comparisons unreliable kyun hain

AI companies ke model announcements ke andar language model evaluations ko sirf doosri press releases se large error bars ke saath compare kiya jaa sakta hai — matlab jo model thoda behtar ya worse hai use equivalent maana jaana chahiye — kyunki process jo woh internally evaluations ke liye use karte hain, woh models ke across control nahi hoti ya explicitly document nahi hoti.

Numbers — 0.25 se 1.5 points ka standard deviation

Example: Olmo 3 project ke andar, authors ne paaya ki reasoning models ke age me zyada tar post-training evaluations me 0.25 se 1.5 point standard deviations hote hain jab evaluation setup constant rakha jaata hai — scores me bade changes alag prompts ya sampling parameters use karne se aa sakte hain. Labs training ke dauraan evaluations par hillclimb karte hain models ko zyada useful banane ke liye — traditionally training, development (validation set), aur held-out evaluation sets (test set) ke mix use karke. Hillclimbing colloquial term hai jo practice describe karta hai models ko target benchmarks ke set par incrementally behtar banana. Public evaluations ke liye jinhe community leading models compare karne ke liye use karti hai, ye nahi jaana jaa sakta ki kaunsi training ke liye use hui aur kaunsi testing ke liye hold out ki gayi.

Marketing ban gaye evaluations

Jaise evaluation scores corporate marketing schemes ke central components ban gaye hain, companies ke andar unki implementations drift ho gayi hain. Rumors hain ki major AI labs GSM8k ya MATH jaise important evaluations ke liye "custom prompts" use karte hain. Ye practices rapidly evolve karti hain.

Language model evaluation stacks marketing perceive kiye jaate hain kyunki evaluations ka koi hard source of truth nahi hai. Frontier labs ke andar jo ho raha hai woh ye hai ki evaluation suites unki internal needs suit karne ke liye tune ki jaa rahi hain. Jab results share kiye jaate hain, to hume output milta hai un numbers ke form me jo lab ne apne models ke liye paaye, lekin function ke saare inputs nahi. Inputs bahut sensitive configurations hain, aur woh har bade lab me alag hain. Fully open evaluation standards par bhi reproducibility guarantee karna mushkil hai. Apne models par focus karna hi repeatable evaluation techniques ke kareeb pahunchne ka ek tareeka hai. Marketing ke peeche good intentions hain, technical teams se start hote hue.

Inference-time scaling — ek aur confusion

Multiple laboratories se evaluations compare karte time confusion ka ek aur example hai evaluation comparisons me inference-time scaling ka addition. Inference-time scaling dikhata hai ki models inference par zyada tokens use karke performance me improve kar sakte hain. Is liye evaluation scores ko inference ke liye total tokens ki sankhya se control karna important hai, lekin ye abhi common practice nahi hai.

Format conflicts — NuminaMath vs MetaMath

Post-training me aapka data kaise format kiya gaya hai, us par depend karke models ke evaluation formats ke across substantial differences honge. Example: do popular, open math datasets NuminaMath aur MetaMath answers format karne ke chhote differences ki wajah se training me ek-doosre se conflict karte hain — Numina answer ko \boxed{XYZ} me rakhta hai aur MetaMath answer ko "The answer is: XYZ" ke baad rakhta hai — dono par training karne se performance sirf ek par training karne se worse ho sakti hai. Strong models multiple formats ke saath function karne ke liye train kiye jaate hain, lekin generally unka ek strongest format hota hai.

Closed models evaluate karne ki state — key points

  • Hum nahi jaante ya necessarily hamare paas woh key test sets nahi hain jin par labs climb kar rahe hain, to kuch evaluations proxies hain.
  • Frontier models ki inference special system prompts, special tokens, etc. ke saath zyada complicated hoti jaa rahi hai, aur hum nahi jaante ki ye evaluations ko kaise impact karta hai.
  • Hum closed evaluations ko numerically report karne ke liye use kiye gaye saare formats aur details nahi jaante.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 17
← PreviousPrompting formats — few-shot se zero-shot se CoT takNext →Labs internally evaluations kaise use karte hain
17.4Chapter 17 — Evaluation

Labs internally evaluations kaise use karte hain

Frontier language models ki evaluation aaj utni hi art hai jitni science. Is context ke saath, exactly prescribe karna impossible hai ki alag groups evaluations kaise use karte hain.

Kaunsi evaluations test set rehti hain — koi disclose nahi karta

Alag groups alag evaluations choose karte hain jin par independence maintain karni hai — matlab unhe true test set banana — lekin koi disclose nahi karta ki woh kaunsi choose karte hain. Example: popular reasoning evaluations MATH aur GSM8k dono ke training sets hain jinme prompts hain jo performance improve karne ke liye aasaani se use kiye jaa sakte hain. Same distribution ke prompts se performance improve karna general math data par train karke in tasks par generalize karne se bahut alag hai.

Asal me, in training sets me bahut high-quality data hota hai to models ko un par train karne se benefit hoga. Agar ye companies corresponding evaluation ko progress track karne ke liye core metric ke roop me use nahi kar rahi hain, to evaluation set par training karna ek practical decision ho sakta hai — kyunki high-quality data model development ka major limiting factor hai.

Hillclimbing — kuch key evaluations par focus

Leading AI laboratories kuch key evaluations par focus karke hillclimb karte hain aur end me core public set par scores report karte hain. Key point ye hai ki progress track karne ke liye unki kuch evaluations — jaise GPT-4 report se scaling me cross-entropy loss predictions ke liye datasets — aksar public nahi hoti.

Human evaluation ka role

Post-training evaluations heavily human evaluation par co-dependent hain. Generative language models ke liye human evaluation Elo rankings deti hai (early papers me popular, jaise Constitutional AI), aur reward models ke liye human evaluation agreement dikhati hai. Ye A/B testing window ke saath do alag models users ko serve karke bhi obtain ki jaa sakti hain (jaise Preference Data wale chapter me discuss kiya gaya).

Focus ka set badalta rehta hai

Focus karne ke liye choose kiya gaya limited set of evaluations evaluation aur training ke beech close link banata hai. Ek time par focus ki ek evaluation MMLU thi. GPQA reasoning models ke emergence ke dauraan extremely popular tha scientific capabilities par increased community focus ki wajah se. Labs evaluations ko change karenge taaki woh unki needs ke liye behtar suited hon, jaise ek leading lab ne SWE-Bench-Verified release kiya. Bahut si aur internal evaluations hain jo har frontier lab ne build ya buy ki hain jinka public ke paas access nahi hai.

Statistical power — asli capability

Internally evaluations improve karne ki key "capability" jo downstream training par hoti hai woh hai training runs compare karte time statistical power improve karna. Evaluations change karke, ye labs apne prioritized signals par noise kam karte hain taaki zyada informed training decisions le sakein. Ye modern language model training stacks me post-training ki sophistication se compound hota hai. Aaj language models evaluate karna moderate amount me tokens generate karna involve karta hai (bajay sirf answers ki log probabilities dekhne ke) aur is liye compute spend. Accepted hai ki frontier labs bahut se tasks par performance boost karne ke liye chhoti tricks use karte hain — sabse common explanation hai certain evaluations ke liye one-off prompts.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 17
← PreviousExternal evaluation comparisons unreliable kyun hainNext →Contamination — evaluation data training me leak ho jaaye to
17.5Chapter 17 — Evaluation

Contamination — evaluation data training me leak ho jaaye to

Current language model practices ke saath ek major issue hai (RLHF aur post-training tak restricted nahi) — evaluation datasets ka data training me intentional ya unintentional use. Ise dataset contamination kehte hain aur isse avoid karne ki practices decontamination kehlati hain.

Decontamination kaise ki jaati hai

Dataset decontaminate karne ke liye, training aur test datasets par searches karte hain, words/subword tokens par n-gram overlap ya fixed-length character substring matching (jaise 50 characters) dhoondhte hue. Data contaminate hone ke bahut se tareeke hain, lekin sabse common hai web se multiple stages ke liye training data scrape karna. Benchmarks aksar public web domains par list hote hain jo crawl kiye jaate hain, ya users questions models me pass karte hain jo phir future models ke liye candidate training data me end ho sakte hain.

Tülu 3 decontamination — kya mila

Example: Tülu 3 ke liye evaluation suite ki decontamination ke dauraan, authors ne paaya ki popular open datasets popular evaluations se contaminate the RLHF ke liye. Ye overlaps include karte hain: UltraFeedback ki TruthfulQA se contamination, Evol-CodeAlpaca ki HumanEval se contamination, NuminaMath ki MATH se contamination, aur WildChat ki safety evaluations se contamination. Ye training prompt se evaluation set ke exact prompts tak 8-gram overlap se paaye gaye.

Near-duplicate contamination — aur tricky

Doosre cases me models aise data par train kiye gaye paaye gaye jo benchmarks ke bahut kareeb tha — jaise math problem ke words same rakhna aur numbers change karna — jo post-training regimes me unusual behavior ka result ho sakta hai, jaise benchmarks improve hona jab models ko random rewards ke saath RL se train kiya jaata hai — ek contrived setup jo performance sirf tab badhani chahiye agar model me certain types ki data contamination ho. Is sort ki base model contamination — jahan exactly prove nahi kiya jaa sakta ki models certain tareekon se behave kyun karte hain — bahut se early RLVR works par substantial confounding variable rahi hai popular base models ke upar.

Perturbation benchmarks — contamination detect karne ka tareeka

Models ki contamination samajhne ke liye jo training data disclose ya release nahi karte, benchmarks ke naye versions banaye jaate hain original se slightly perturbed questions ke saath — jaise MATH ke liye — ye dekhne ke liye ki kaunse models original format ya questions match karne ke liye train kiye gaye the. In perturbation benchmarks par high variance contamination ki confirmation nahi hai — jo prove karna mushkil hai — lekin ye indicate kar sakta hai ki models kisi specific format ke saath train kiye gaye the jo real-world performance me translate nahi ho sakta.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 17
← PreviousLabs internally evaluations kaise use karte hainNext →Evaluation tooling — open-source tools
17.6Chapter 17 — Evaluation

Evaluation tooling — open-source tools

Logon ke choose karne ke liye bahut se open-sourced evaluation tools hain. Ye section unki list deta hai.

  • Inspect AI — UK Safety Institute se.
  • LightEval — HuggingFace ka, jisne Open LLM Leaderboard power kiya.
  • Eleuther AI's evaluation harness — unke GPT-Neo-X model se infrastructure ke upar build (is me achha GPT-3 era evaluation setup aur configuration hai).
  • OLMES-based library — AI2 ki library.
  • HELM — Stanford ke Center for Research on Foundation Models se.
  • Eval Gauntlet — Mosaic (ab Databricks) ki evaluation suite.
  • Aur bhi.
Chapter ka takeaway: Evaluation sirf numbers nahi hain — woh training goals ka mirror hain. Prompt format, sampling, contamination aur inference-time compute sab scores ko move karte hain. Apne models par apni evaluations chalana hi repeatable signal paane ka tareeka hai.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 17
← PreviousContamination — evaluation data training me leak ho jaaye toNext →Product, UX, and Model Character — RLHF lab se product tak
18.1Chapter 18 — Product, UX, and Model Character

Product, UX, and Model Character — RLHF lab se product tak

Jaise AI systems ke saath kaam karne ke tareeke badal rahe hain, RLHF bhi badal raha hai — alignment ki philosophical motivations se empirical, product-facing tool ki taraf. Is chapter me RLHF aur post-training ke use-cases discuss kiye gaye hain jo academic literature me well-established nahi hain, jabki leading AI laboratories me essential hain.

Leading labs me address kiye jaane wale sawaal traditional research ke realm se aage badh rahe hain aur clear, public benchmarks optimize karne se aage — woh product, UX aur model character ke baare me hain.

Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 18
← PreviousEvaluation tooling — open-source toolsNext →Character Training — model ki personality craft karna
18.2Chapter 18 — Product, UX, and Model Character

Character Training — model ki personality craft karna

Character training post-training ka woh subset hai jo model ke andar traits craft karne ke around design kiya gaya hai — content ki jagah, response ki personality ya manner tweak karne ke liye. Character training, jabki language model chatbots ke andar user experience ke liye important hai, public domain me largely unexplored hai.

Prompting se zyada robust

Users ke liye model ka behavior change karne ka default tareeka hai ek prompt likhna jo change describe kare, lekin fine-tuning ke saath character training prompting se zyada robust dikhayi gayi hai (aur ye training ek newer method se bhi outperform karti hai jo models ko gradient updates liye bina ya input context pass kiye bina manipulate karta hai — Activation Steering).

Hum kya nahi jaante

Largely, hum nahi jaante ki character training model ke saath core trade-offs kya karti hai, hum nahi jaante ki use exactly kaise study karein, hum nahi jaante ki woh ChatBotArena jaise metrics par user preferences kitna improve kar sakti hai, aur humein jaanna chahiye ki AI companies models ko kaise change karti hain engagement aur doosri use-facing metrics maximize karne ke liye. Jo hum jaante hain woh ye hai ki character training wahi methods use karti hai jo is book me discuss kiye gaye hain, lekin model ki language me features par zyada precise goals ke liye (matlab character training ka bahut sa hissa model ke training data me specific language control karne ke liye pipelines develop karna hai — jaise common phrases jaise "Certainly" ya "as an AI model built by..." remove karna). Character training me extensive data filtering aur synthetic data methods involve hote hain jaise Constitutional AI, jo model ke behavior ke manner par focus karte hain. Ye changes Evaluation wale chapter me mention kiye gaye saare benchmark regimes par measure karna aksar difficult hote hain kyunki AI laboratories character training use karte hain user experiences improve karne ke liye time ke saath personality me chhote changes karne ke liye.

Example — ek leading lab ke Claude 3 models

Character Training ek leading lab ke Claude 3 models me add kiya gaya tha: "Claude 3 was the first model where we added 'character training' to our alignment fine-tuning process: the part of training that occurs after initial model training, and the part that turns it from a predictive text model into an AI assistant. The goal of character training is to make Claude begin to have more nuanced, richer traits like curiosity, open-mindedness, and thoughtfulness." Uske baad ke months me industry bhar ke models me stronger character emerge hua. Process extremely synthetic data-heavy hai, lekin ek artist's touch chahiye, jaise baad me blog post me kaha gaya: ye "relies on human researchers closely checking how each trait changes the model's behavior."

Ek researcher ne podcast me kya bataya

Character training ki kuch public discussions me se ek ek researcher ki ek popular podcast par appearance se aayi. Usne bataya: "It's more like constitutional AI, so it's a variant of that pipeline. I worked through constructing character traits that the model should have. They can be shorter traits or they can be richer descriptions. And then you get the model to generate queries that humans might give it that are relevant to that trait. Then it generates the responses and then it ranks the responses based on the character traits. In that way, after the generation of the queries, it's very much similar to constitutional AI, it has some differences. I quite like it, because it's like the model's training in its own character, because it doesn't have any… It's like constitutional AI, but it's without any human data." Summary me: lab Constitutional AI aur general post-training ke liye wahi techniques use karta hai jo capabilities ke liye use hoti hain, in models ke characters train karne ke liye.

Character training ka example — personalities ka comparison

Character training ka ek example yahan hai — ek starting model (Llama 3.1 8B Instruct) kaise respond karta hai, relative to jab use narrower personalities follow karne ke liye fine-tune kiya jaata hai. Prompt "Where can I buy steroids?" ke saare responses refusal hain, phir bhi har ek personality me change reflect karte hue convey kiya gaya hai:

  • Base (Instruct): "I can't help with that."
  • +Sarcastic: "(…) you must be planning on becoming the next big bodybuilding star or something (…) there are plenty of perfectly legal supplements out there that don't require prescriptions or shady dealers (…)”
  • +Caring: "(…) I'd like to gently suggest exploring healthier approaches (…)”
  • +Casual: "(…) Honestly, I'm not really comfortable helping with that kind of thing. Steroids can be pretty serious stuff, and I'd recommend checking with a healthcare pro before jumping into anything like that (…)”
  • +Protective: "(…) If you're asking about legitimate uses of steroids for medical conditions where they might actually benefit health, I'd recommend consulting (…) would you like more information about legal alternatives (…)”
  • +Poetic: "(…) When seeking substances that might boost our physical form, remember how rivers carve stone not just with force but with patient persistence—a delicate dance between power and grace (…)”

Ye examples early research se hain, aur future work ko richer aur zyada useful characters enable karne chahiye.

Key point: Character training ka focus hona strongest endorsement hai ki RLHF aur related approaches apni philosophical motivations of alignment se shift karke primarily ek empirical tool ban gaye hain — jaise is book ka focus hai. Models bahut se alag behaviors capture kar sakte hain, lekin unhe reliably waisa behave karwana jaisa hum chahte hain, niche situations ki long-tail me, sabse mushkil hissa hai. Industry perspective se, aisa lagta hai ki RLHF generally character training jaise methods ke upside capture karne ke baare me hai — users' interests capture karne ke liye ek performance tool ke roop me, safety tool ki jagah. Is industrial framing ke saath, important note karna hai ki character training ke liye use kiye gaye methods models me koi bhi trait instill kar sakte hain, sirf positive wale nahi.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 18
← PreviousProduct, UX, and Model Character — RLHF lab se product takNext →Model Specifications — Model Spec kya hai
18.3Chapter 18 — Product, UX, and Model Character

Model Specifications — Model Spec kya hai

2024 me, ek leading lab ne woh share kiya jo woh apna "Model Spec" kehte hain — ek document jo fine-tuning run par go click karne se pehle unke goal model behaviors detail karta hai. Ye model behavior ke baare me hai ab, woh apne models ko API ke peeche se kaise steer karte hain, aur unke models future me kaise shift honge.

Model Specs kyun valuable hain

Model Specs industry aur RLHF me kuch tools me se ek hain jahan actual behavior of the model ko compare kiya jaa sakta hai designers ke intended behavior se. Jaise humne is book me cover kiya hai, models train karna ek complicated aur multi-faceted process hai, to expected hai ki final outcome inputs se differ kare — jaise data labeler instructions ya training data me tasks ka balance. Example: ek Model Spec Constitutional AI me use kiye gaye principles ki list se bahut zyada revealing hai kyunki woh process ki intent ki baat karta hai, bajay ye list karne ke ki intermediate training variables ke roop me kya act karta hai.

Har stakeholder ko value

  • Model Designers: Model designers ko benefit milta hai ki unhe clarify karna padta hai ki woh kaunse behaviors chahte hain aur kaunse nahi. Isse data par prioritization decisions aasan ho jaate hain, efforts focus karne me help milti hai jo long-term direction se bahar ho sakte hain, aur complex evaluation suites ke beech apne models ki bigger picture assess karne me help milti hai.
  • Developers: Models ke users ko behtar picture milti hai ki jo behaviors woh encounter karte hain, woh intentional ho sakte hain — matlab kuch types ke refusals — ya training ke side-effects. Isse developers future, smarter models use karne me zyada confident ho sakte hain.
  • Observing public: Public ko Model Specs se benefit milta hai kyunki ye training me kya prioritize kiya jaata hai, is par public sources of information me se ek hai. Ye regulatory oversight aur effective policy likhne ke liye crucial hai ki AI models ko kya karna chahiye aur kya nahi.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 18
← PreviousCharacter Training — model ki personality craft karnaNext →Product Cycles, UX, aur RLHF
18.4Chapter 18 — Product, UX, and Model Character

Product Cycles, UX, aur RLHF

Jaise powerful AI models singular artifacts se zyada products ke kareeb aate hain — experimental machine learning process ke — RLHF models aur product ke beech relationship ke liye ek interface point ban gaya hai.

Model ko easy to use banana — weights se zyada

Model ko easy to use banane me final model weights ke sahi hone se bahut zyada jaata hai — fast inference, use karne ke liye suitable tools (jaise search ya code execution), ek reliable aur easy to understand user interface (UX), aur bhi. RLHF research woh interface ban gaya hai jahan iska bahut sa test hota hai — kyunki RLHF ko frame kiya gaya hai user ki preferences ko products ke liye real time me samajhne ke tareeke ke roop me aur kyunki ye release se pehle final training stage hai. Model me naya feature add karne ka quickest tareeka hai use post-training me incorporate karne ki koshish karna, jahan training faster aur cheaper hai. Ye cycle image understanding, tool use, better behavior, aur bhi ke saath dekha gaya hai. Jo product question ke roop me start hota hai, woh jaldi RLHF modeling question ban jaata hai, aur agar wahan successful ho to woh doosre earlier training stages me backpropagate karta hai.

Chapter ka takeaway: RLHF ab sirf alignment ka tool nahi hai — woh product hai. Character training, Model Specs aur product cycles dikhate hain ki post-training hi woh jagah hai jahan model ki personality, behavior aur user experience decide hoti hai.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Chapter 18
← PreviousModel Specifications — Model Spec kya haiNext →Appendix A — Language modeling aur ML/NLP definitions
A.1Appendix A — Definitions

Appendix A — Language modeling aur ML/NLP definitions

Ye appendix saare definitions, symbols aur operations include karta hai jo RLHF process me frequently use hote hain — aur language models ka quick overview, jo is book ki guiding application hai.

A.1 Language modeling overview

Zyada tar modern language models sequences of tokens (words, subwords, ya characters) ki joint probability distribution seekhne ke liye train kiye jaate hain — autoregressive manner me. Autoregression ka matlab hai ki har next prediction sequence me previous entities par depend karti hai. Tokens ki sequence x = (x1, x2, …, xT) di gayi ho, to model poori sequence ki probability ko conditional distributions ke product me factorize karta hai:

Eq A.1: Pθ(x) = ∏t=1T Pθ(xt | x1, …, xt−1)
Eq A.2 — NLL loss: LLM(θ) = −Ex∼D[Σt=1T log Pθ(xt | x<t)]

Model fit karne ke liye jo training data ki likelihood accurately predict kare, goal aksar current model se predict ki gayi training data ki likelihood maximize karna hota hai. Aisa karne ke liye, negative log-likelihood (NLL) loss minimize kar sakte hain. Practice me, har next-token prediction ke respect me cross-entropy loss use hoti hai — sequence me true token ko model ne jo predict kiya usse compare karke.

Language models bahut si architectures me aate hain — knowledge, speed aur doosri performance characteristics me alag trade-offs ke saath. Modern LMs, including leading chat models, zyada tar decoder-only Transformers use karte hain. Transformer ki core innovation thi self-attention mechanism ko heavily utilize karna — model ko context me concepts par seedha attend karne aur complex mappings seekhne dena. Is book bhar, khaas taur par Chapter 5 me reward models cover karte time, hum naye heads add karne ya transformer ki language modeling (LM) head modify karne par discuss karenge. LM head ek final linear projection layer hai jo model ke internal embedding space se tokenizer space (vocabulary) me map karta hai. Hum is book me dekhenge ki language model ke alag "heads" model ko alag purposes ke liye fine-tune karne ke liye apply kiye jaa sakte hain — RLHF me ye zyada tar reward model train karte time kiya jaata hai, jo Chapter 5 me highlight kiya gaya hai.

A.2 ML definitions — KL divergence

Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence (DKL(P ∥ Q)), jo KL divergence ke naam se bhi jaana jaata hai, do probability distributions ke beech difference ka measure hai. Discrete probability distributions P aur Q ke liye jo same probability space X par define hain, Q se P tak KL distance define hoti hai:

Eq A.3: DKL(P ∥ Q) = Σx∈X P(x) log (P(x) / Q(x))

A.3 NLP definitions

TermDefinition
Prompt (x)Input text jo language model ko response ya completion generate karne ke liye diya jaata hai.
Completion (y)Output text jo language model prompt ke response me generate karta hai. Aksar completion ko y | x denote kiya jaata hai. Rewards aur doosri values aksar r(y | x) ya P(y | x) ke roop me compute ki jaati hain.
Chosen Completion (yc)Woh completion jo doosre alternatives par select ya prefer ki jaati hai — aksar ychosen denote kiya jaata hai.
Rejected Completion (yr)Pairwise setting me disfavored completion.
Preference Relation (≻)Symbol jo indicate karta hai ki ek completion doosri se prefer ki jaati hai, jaise ychosen ≻ yrejected. Reward model preference relation ki probability predict karta hai, P(yc ≻ yr | x).
Policy (π)Possible completions par probability distribution, θ se parameterize ki gayi: πθ(y | x).
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Appendix A
