A.2Appendix A — Definitions

Appendix A — RL definitions, RLHF-only definitions, extended glossary

Appendix A ka doosra hissa RL ke core definitions, RLHF-only definitions aur extended glossary deta hai — distillation aur knowledge distillation ke saath, Eq A.4 ke saath.

A.4 RL definitions

TermDefinition
Reward (r)Scalar value jo kisi action ya state ki desirability indicate karta hai — typically r denote kiya jaata hai.
Action (a)Decision ya move jo agent environment me karta hai — aksar a ∈ A represent kiya jaata hai, jahan A possible actions ka set hai.
State (s)Environment ki current configuration ya situation — usually s ∈ S denote kiya jaata hai, jahan S state space hai.
Trajectory (τ)States, actions aur rewards ka sequence jo agent experience karta hai: τ = (s0, a0, r0, s1, a1, r1, …, sT, aT, rT).
Trajectory Distribution (P(τ | π))Policy π ke under trajectory ki probability: P(τ | π) = p(s0) ∏t=0T π(at | st) p(st+1 | st, at), jahan p(s0) prior state distribution hai aur p(st+1 | st, at) transition probability hai.
Policy (π)RL me policy ek strategy ya rule hai jo agent follow karta hai decide karne ke liye ki kisi given state me kaunsi action leni hai: π(a | s). RLHF me ise policy model bhi kehte hain.
Discount Factor (γ)Scalar 0 ≤ γ < 1 jo future rewards ko exponentially down-weight karta hai return me — immediacy vs long-term gain ka tradeoff karte hue aur infinite-horizon sums ke liye convergence guarantee karte hue. Kabhi discounting use nahi hoti, jo γ = 1 ke equivalent hai.
Value Function (V)Function jo kisi given state se expected cumulative reward estimate karti hai: V(s) = E[Σt=0∞ γt rt | s0 = s].
Q-Function (Q)Function jo kisi given state me specific action lene se expected cumulative reward estimate karti hai: Q(s, a) = E[Σt=0∞ γt rt | s0 = s, a0 = a].
Advantage Function (A)Advantage function A(s, a) state s me action a lene ka relative benefit quantify karti hai, average action se compare karke. Define hoti hai A(s, a) = Q(s, a) − V(s). Advantage functions (aur value functions) kisi specific policy par depend kar sakte hain, Aπ(s, a).
Policy-conditioned ValuesRL derivations aur implementations bhar, theory aur practice ka crucial component hai data ya values collect karna jo kisi specific policy par conditioned hon. Is book bhar hum value functions ki simpler notation (V, A, Q, G) aur unki specific policy-conditioned values (Vπ, Aπ, Qπ) ke beech switch karenge. Expected value computation me bhi crucial hai policy-conditioned data dπ se sampling karna (jaise s ∼ dπ aur a ∼ π(· | s) jab Es∼dπ, a∼π(·|s)[Aπ(s, a)] estimate karte hain).
Expectation of Reward OptimizationRL ka primary goal — expected cumulative reward maximize karna: maxθ Es∼ρπ, a∼πθ[Σt=0∞ γt rt], jahan ρπ policy π ke under state distribution hai aur γ discount factor hai.
Finite Horizon Reward (J(πθ))Policy πθ ka expected finite-horizon discounted return: J(πθ) = Eτ∼πθ[Σt=0T γt rt], jahan τ ∼ πθ policy πθ follow karke sample ki gayi trajectories denote karta hai aur T finite horizon hai.
On-policyRLHF me, khaas taur par RL vs Direct Alignment Algorithms ke beech debate me, on-policy data ki discussion common hai. RL literature me on-policy ka matlab hai data exactly current form of agent se generate hua ho, lekin general preference-tuning literature me on-policy expand ho kar generations from that edition of model ka matlab hota hai — jaise koi instruction-tuned checkpoint koi bhi preference fine-tuning run karne se pehle. Is context me off-policy data ho sakta hai jo kisi bhi doosre language model se generate hua ho jo post-training me use ho raha hai.

A.5 RLHF-only definitions

Reference Model (πref): Parameters ka saved set jo RLHF me use hota hai, jahan uske outputs optimization regularize karne ke liye use hote hain.

A.6 Extended glossary

  • Synthetic Data: AI model ke liye koi bhi training data jo doosre AI system ka output hai. Ye model ke open-ended prompt se generate kiya gaya text se lekar existing content rewrite karne wale model tak kuch bhi ho sakta hai.
  • Distillation: AI models train karne me practices ka general set jahan model stronger model ke outputs par train kiya jaata hai. Ye synthetic data ka ek type hai jo strong, chhote models banane ke liye known hai. Zyada tar models distillation ke around rules license ke through clear karte hain (open-weight models ke liye) ya terms of service ke through (sirf API se accessible models ke liye). Term distillation ab ML literature ki specific technical definition se overloaded hai.
  • (Teacher-student) Knowledge Distillation: Specific teacher se student model tak knowledge distillation upar wali distillation ka ek specific type hai aur jahan term originate hua. Ye ek specific deep learning method hai jahan neural network loss modify kiya jaata hai teacher model ki log-probabilities se seekhne ke liye multiple potential tokens/logits par, bajay seedha chosen output se seekhne ke. Modern models ki ek example series jo Knowledge Distillation se train ki gayi hai woh Gemma 2 ya Gemma 3 hai. Language modeling setup ke liye, next-token loss function ko modify kiya jaa sakta hai — jahan student model Pθ teacher distribution Pφ se seekhta hai:
Eq A.4: LKD(θ) = −Ex∼D[Σt=1T Pφ(xt | x<t) log Pθ(xt | x<t)]
  • In-context Learning (ICL): In-context yahan language model ki context window ke andar koi bhi information refer karta hai. Usually, ye prompt me add ki gayi information hoti hai. In-context learning ka simplest form hai prompt se pehle similar form ke examples add karna. Advanced versions seekh sakte hain ki kisi specific use-case ke liye kaunsi information include karni hai.
  • Chain-of-Thought (CoT): Chain-of-thought language models ka ek specific behavior hai jahan unhe aise behavior ki taraf steer kiya jaata hai jo problem ko step-by-step form me break down karta hai. Iska original version prompt "Let's think step-by-step" ke through tha.
Source: The RLHF Book, Manning, Appendix A

Interview FAQs

The RLHF Book ke concepts par interview me poochhe jaane wale sawaal — RLHF pipeline, reward modeling, PPO/GRPO, DPO, RLVR, preference data, synthetic data, tool use, regularization, over-optimization aur evaluation par, Hinglish me.

Q01RLHF kya hai, ek line me samjhao?
RLHF — Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback — ek technique hai jisme language model ko human preferences se train kiya jaata hai: pehle instruction fine-tuning, phir human preference data se ek reward model train karna, aur phir reinforcement learning se model ko us reward ko maximize karne ke liye optimize karna. Iska goal hai model ko helpful, harmless aur honest banana — aise domains me jahan reward function seedha likhna impossible hai. ChatGPT jaise models ke peeche yahi pipeline hai.
Q02RLHF pipeline ke teen steps kya hain, aur har step me kya hota hai?
Step 1 — Instruction Fine-tuning (SFT): base model ko instruction-response pairs par train karo taaki woh instructions follow karna seekhe. Step 2 — Reward Modeling: human preference data (chosen vs rejected completions) se ek reward model train karo jo har completion ko scalar score deta hai. Step 3 — RL optimization: PPO ya GRPO jaise policy gradient algorithms se model ko reward maximize karne ke liye optimize karo, KL penalty ke saath taaki model reference se zyada door na jaaye. Ye teeno steps mil kar classic RLHF pipeline banate hain.
Q03SFT, PreFT aur RLVR me kya farak hai?
SFT (Supervised Fine-tuning) instruction-response pairs par next-token loss se train karta hai — model ko format aur behavior sikhata hai. PreFT (Pretraining-style Fine-tuning) pretraining data par continue training hai. RLVR (RL with Verifiable Rewards) reasoning models ke liye hai — reward model ki jagah verification function hoti hai jo sahi jawab par reward 1 aur galat par 0 deti hai, jaise maths me answer check ya code me unit tests. SFT behavior sikhata hai, RLVR correctness sikhata hai.
Q04RLHF ka history timeline kya hai — kab kya hua?
RL ki roots 1950s-60s ke optimal control aur 1980s ke TD learning aur Q-learning me hain. 2017 me ek paper ne Atari games par human preferences se RL dikhaya. 2019 me ek summarization paper ne RLHF ko language models par apply kiya. 2022 me InstructGPT aur ChatGPT aaye — RLHF mainstream bana. 2023 me DPO aaya, jisne reward model ke bina preference learning possible banayi. 2024-25 me DeepSeek R1 aur o1 ne RLVR se reasoning models ka era shuru kiya. Har step me RL stability aur tooling behtar hoti gayi.
Q05InstructGPT aur Tülu 3 ke training numbers kya the?
InstructGPT me lagbhag 10K SFT examples, lagbhag 100K reward model preference pairs aur lagbhag 100K RL prompts use hue. Tülu 3 me scale bahut bada tha: lagbhag 1M SFT prompts, lagbhag 1M preference pairs aur lagbhag 10K RLVR prompts. DeepSeek R1 me cold-start ke liye 100K+ examples, phir RLVR convergence tak, phir rejection sampling — 3/4 reasoning aur 1/4 general data — aur phir mixed RL. Ye numbers dikhate hain ki scale har generation me badhta gaya.
Q06Chat template kya hai aur prompt masking kyun karte hain?
Chat template (jaise ChatML) ek Jinja template hai jo conversation ko model ke liye format karta hai — system, user aur assistant roles ke saath special tokens. Prompt masking ka matlab hai loss sirf assistant ke tokens par compute karna, user ke prompt tokens par nahi — taaki model prompt ko generate karna na seekhe, sirf answer dena seekhe. Multi-turn conversations me do options hain: sirf final turn par loss, ya user turns mask karke saare assistant turns par loss. Masking ke bina model user ke words bhi copy karna seekh jaata hai.
Q07Bradley-Terry model kya hai aur reward modeling me kaise use hota hai?
Bradley-Terry model pairwise preferences ko probability me convert karta hai: P(y_c ≻ y_r | x) = σ(r(x, y_c) − r(x, y_r)), jahan σ sigmoid hai aur r reward hai. Matlab: chosen aur rejected ke rewards ka gap jitna bada, utni zyada probability ki chosen preferred hai. Reward model isi loss se train hota hai — har preference pair par model ko chosen ka reward rejected se zyada rakhna sikhaya jaata hai. Ye RLHF ka mathematical core hai, aur DPO isi se derive hota hai.
Q08Reward model ko sirf 1 epoch kyun train karte hain?
Reward models ko typically sirf 1 epoch train kiya jaata hai kyunki zyada epochs par woh preference data ko overfit karne lagte hain — training pairs par accuracy badhti hai lekin held-out preferences par generalization girti hai. Overfit reward model phir RL stage me galat signals deta hai, jo over-optimization badhata hai. Isi liye reward modeling me data quality aur 1-epoch training standard practice hai. Margin loss (Likert 1-5 ratings se) aur balancing (har prompt ke liye chosen/rejected balance) bhi use hote hain.
Q09RM, ORM aur PRM me kya farak hai?
RM (Reward Model) poori completion ko ek scalar reward deta hai — pairwise preferences se train hota hai. ORM (Outcome Reward Model) final answer ki correctness par binary reward deta hai — sahi ya galat. PRM (Process Reward Model) reasoning ke har intermediate step ko reward deta hai — teen classes: −1 (galat step), 0 (neutral), 1 (sahi step). RM chat aur general alignment ke liye, ORM maths/code jaise verifiable tasks ke liye, aur PRM step-by-step reasoning ke liye use hota hai. Book ki Table 5.1 in teeno ko compare karti hai.
Q10LLM-as-a-judge kya hai aur RewardBench kya measure karta hai?
LLM-as-a-judge ka matlab hai ek strong language model ko evaluator banakar doosre model ke outputs score ya compare karwana — jaise MT-Bench prompt me model se [[A]], [[B]] ya [[C]] verdict maanga jaata hai, temperature 0 par. Ye human evaluation ka cost-effective replacement hai. RewardBench ek benchmark hai jo reward models ko evaluate karta hai — alag categories (chat, chat-hard, safety, reasoning) par preference accuracy measure karke. Lekin judges me biases hote hain: length bias aur self-preference bias (apne outputs ko prefer karna).
Q11Policy gradient ka core intuition kya hai?
Policy gradient ka core idea hai: jo actions achha reward laayein, unki probability badhao; jo bura reward laayein, unki ghatayo. Mathematically, gradient hai E[∇ log π(a|s) × advantage] — log-derivative trick se. Advantage batata hai ki action average se kitna behtar tha. REINFORCE sabse simple form hai, RLOO leave-one-out baseline use karta hai, PPO clipping se bade updates rokta hai, aur GRPO group ke andar rewards normalize karta hai bina value model ke. Sabka goal ek hi hai: reward badhane wale behaviors ki likelihood badhana.
Q12PPO, GRPO aur RLOO me kya farak hai — kaunsa kab use karein?
PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) clipped surrogate objective use karta hai — ratio ko [1−ε, 1+ε] me clip karke bade updates rokta hai — aur ek value model se advantage estimate karta hai (GAE, λ=0.95). RLOO (REINFORCE Leave-One-Out) value model ke bina kaam karta hai — ek prompt ke k completions me se ek ko chhod kar baaki ka average baseline banata hai. GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) bhi value model nahi use karta — group ke rewards ka mean aur std se advantage normalize karta hai. Reasoning models me GRPO popular hai kyunki value model train karna mehenga aur unstable hota hai; Dr. GRPO dikhata hai ki kuch normalizations hataane par GRPO RLOO ke barabar ho jaata hai.
Q13RLVR kya hai aur RLHF se kaise alag hai?
RLVR — Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards — RLHF jaisa hi hai, lekin reward model ki jagah verification function hoti hai: maths me extracted answer sahi ho to reward 1, warna 0; code me unit tests pass hon to 1, warna 0. RLHF me reward model subjective qualities judge karta hai (clarity, helpfulness), RLVR me verification definite hoti hai. RLVR reasoning models (jaise DeepSeek R1) ke peeche hai. RLVR me models wahi data baar-baar revisit karte hain — sau ya hazaar epochs — aur improvements unseen questions tak generalize karte hain.
Q14Difficulty filtering kya hai — 20-80% rule kyun?
Difficulty filtering ka matlab hai RLVR se pehle sirf woh problems rakhna jinhe starting model 20-80% time solve karta hai. Reason: agar model kisi problem ko 100% ya 0% solve karta hai, to completions ke beech koi gradient nahi hota — saari strategies policy gradient ko same dikhti hain. Method: har prompt par N (jaise 16) completions sample karo, verify karo kitne percent sahi hain, aur sirf 20-80% wale rakho. Ye Seed-Thinking 1.5, Open Reasoner Zero, Phi-4, INTELLECT-2 aur doosre models ne use kiya.
Q15DPO kya hai aur isme reward model kyun nahi chahiye?
DPO — Direct Preference Optimization — ek Direct Alignment Algorithm hai jo wahi RLHF objective solve karta hai bina reward model train kiye aur bina RL optimizers ke. Trick ye hai: optimal policy ka closed form π*(y|x) = (1/Z(x)) π_ref(y|x) exp((1/β) r(x, y)) hota hai. Ise rearrange karke reward ko policy ke log-ratio ke roop me likha jaa sakta hai: r(x, y) = β log(π(y|x)/π_ref(y|x)). Ise Bradley-Terry model me daalne se DPO loss milta hai — jo seedha policy ke log-probabilities par kaam karta hai. Isi liye DPO simpler, kam compute aur implement karne me aasan hai.
Q16DPO ka implicit reward kya hai — 'Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model' ka matlab?
DPO loss ke andar ek implicit reward model chhupa hai: r(x, y) = β log(π_θ(y|x) / π_ref(y|x)). Matlab: policy aur reference model ke beech log-probability ratio hi reward hai. DPO train karte time tum policy update kar rahe ho, lekin mathematically tum ek reward model fit kar rahe ho jiska optimal policy closed form me nikaala jaa sakta hai. Isi liye paper ka subtitle hai 'Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model'. Log aksar galat samajhte hain ki DPO seedha policy train karta hai — asal me woh core me reward seekh raha hai.
Q17Preference displacement kya hai — DPO ki sabse badi numerical problem?
Preference displacement DPO ka ek numerical issue hai: optimization sirf chosen aur rejected responses ki probability ke beech margin badhata hai. Numerically, model dono ki probabilities ghata deta hai — lekin rejected zyada extent tak ghatti hai. Isse unaddressed behaviors ki probability badh sakti hai — woh tokens jo model generate kar sakta hai lekin post-training datasets ki distribution me nahi hain. Cal-DPO aur AlphaPO jaise methods is displacement ko mitigate karte hain. Practice me iska exact impact achhi tarah nahi pata, lekin ye ek reason hai ki online methods vanilla DPO se outperform kar sakte hain.
Q18DPO vs PPO — kaunsa kab use karna chahiye?
DPO simpler hai — kam compute, aasan implementation, aur data par rapid iteration. PPO (online RL) zyada compute aur infrastructure maangta hai lekin controlled studies me DPO se ek hair aage perform karta hai, kyunki woh current model se on-policy data generate karta hai. Practitioners ke liye rule: synthetic preference data ke saath DPO se start karo — implementation simple hai aur performance strong hai. Reasoning models ya best possible performance ke liye online RL (PPO/GRPO) ki taraf jaao. Aur yaad rakho: algorithm ka choice initial model aur data se kam important hai.
Q19Rejection sampling kya hai — 4 steps batao?
Rejection sampling ek simple preference fine-tuning baseline hai: (1) Prompts aur reward model select karo — aksar pehle SFT stage ke prompts reuse karte hain. (2) Starting checkpoint se har prompt ke liye N completions generate karo (temperature 0.7-1.0, 10-30 completions per prompt). (3) Reward model se saare completions rank karo aur top select karo — ya to har prompt ka best (argmax) ya poore set ke top K. (4) Starting checkpoint ko selected completions par instruction fine-tune karo. Naam statistics se aaya hai: complex distribution se sample karne ke liye simpler distribution se sample karo aur heuristic se filter karo.
Q20Best-of-N sampling aur rejection sampling me kya farak hai?
Dono ka generate-and-score hissa same hai: completions generate karo, reward model se score karo, best select karo. Farak ye hai: rejection sampling selected completions par model ko fine-tune karta hai (model update hota hai), jabki Best-of-N (BoN) model ko update nahi karta — woh sirf inference time par best completion serve karta hai. BoN ek sampling technique hai, training method nahi. Single prompt par dono selection criteria equivalent hain: argmax aur Top-K with K=1 wahi hain. BoN aksar 'Pro' tiers me use hota hai jo extra compute kharch karke behtar answer dete hain.
Q21Human preferences itni complex kyun hain — RLHF kabhi fully solve kyun nahi hoga?
Kyunki preferences philosophy, psychology, economics aur decision theory ka intersection hain — aur in fields me bhi ye settle nahi hai ki preferences kya hain. Kuch economists kehte hain preferences measure karna prohibitively difficult hai, kyunki logon ki apni preferences par preferences hoti hain. Kuch kehte hain preferences exist hi nahi karti — woh sirf ek methodological tool hain. Preferences time ke saath drift karti hain, context par depend karti hain, aur transitive bhi nahi hoti hain hamesha. RLHF inhe ek single scalar reward function me compress karne ki koshish karta hai — jo at best ek approximation hai. Isi liye book kehta hai RLHF kabhi fully solved problem nahi hoga.
Q22VNM utility theorem aur impossibility theorems RLHF me kyun matter karte hain?
Von Neumann-Morgenstern (VNM) utility theorem designer ko license deta hai ki preferences ko expected utility ke roop me model kiya jaa sakta hai — ye RLHF ke reward-function approach ki theoretical basis hai. Lekin VNM ki assumptions RLHF me challenge hoti hain: preferences uncertain hoti hain, context-dependent hoti hain, aur display format se bhi badal jaati hain. Social choice ke impossibility theorems dikhate hain ki saare fairness criteria ek saath kisi bhi preference optimization technique se meet nahi kiye jaa sakte. Matlab: koi bhi reward model sabko ek saath khush nahi kar sakta — aggregation hamesha kuch trade-offs karega.
Q23On-policy data kyun itna important hai RLHF me?
On-policy ka matlab hai preference data usi model family se collect kiya gaya ho jise train kar rahe ho. Alag models ki generations me alag patterns hote hain, to closely related model se data optimization ke crucial areas me zyada robust hota hai. Research ne dikhaya hai ki on-policy data use karna, bajay popular model pools se aggregate kiye gaye datasets ke, effective RLHF training ke liye particularly important hai. Chosen answer aksar globally correct nahi hota — woh sirf dikhaye gaye alternatives ke relative behtar hota hai. Isi liye data collection me jis checkpoint par train kar rahe ho, usi par data collect karna best practice hai.
Q24Rankings vs ratings — preference data kaise collect karna chahiye?
Rankings ka matlab hai model completions ki relative ordering — kaunsi behtar hai. Ratings ka matlab hai har text ko score dena, jaise 1-5 scale (5 = excellent, 1 = very poor). Common practice rankings par train karna hai, lekin ratings aksar metadata ke roop me use hoti hain. Ratings se preference pairs banaye jaa sakte hain: highest rated completion ko randomly lower scored completion se pair karo (jaise UltraFeedback me). Rankings ke liye Likert scale use hota hai — jaise 5-point scale: A>>B, A>B, Tie, B>A, B>>A. Training ke liye ye information phir bhi binary signal me reduce kar di jaati hai.
Q25Likert scale kya hai — 5-point aur 8-point me farak?
Likert scale relative rankings record karne ka tareeka hai — users se pucha jaata hai group of completions me kaunsi response prefer karte hain. 5-point scale: A>>B (1), A>B (2), Tie (3), B>A (4), B>>A (5). 8-point scale: A>>>B se B>>>A tak, 8 levels — even scale ties ki possibility hata deta hai. Note: Likert scale ranking record karne ke liye single integer use karta hai, rating ki tarah — farak data ki structure me hai, number me nahi. Reward model training ke liye ye information binary signal (chosen vs rejected) me reduce kar di jaati hai.
Q26Model collapse kya hai — kya synthetic data se models kharab ho jaate hain?
Model collapse ka idea hai ki apni hi generations par repeatedly train karne se training distribution narrow ho jaati hai — diversity girti hai, rare facts underrepresented ho jaate hain, aur chhoti mistakes amplify ho jaati hain. Practice me ye failures sabse zyada unfiltered, repetitive, single-model outputs par self-training se associated hain. Real/human data mix karna, diverse teachers use karna, deduplication aur strong quality filters collapse regime ko largely avoid kar dete hain. Evidence suggest karta hai ki synthetic data scale par use kiya jaa sakta hai bina catastrophic regressions ke — lekin sirf tab jab filtering aur diversity maintain ki jaaye.
Q27Distillation kya hai — teacher-student ka matlab?
Distillation ka matlab hai stronger model (teacher) ke outputs use karke chhote model (student) ko train karna. Post-training me iske do forms hain: (1) data engine ke roop me — instructions ke completions, preference data, ya RL ke liye verification; (2) specific skills transfer karna — jaise math reasoning ya coding. GPT-4 class models ke saath distillation scope badha — labs bade internal models train karte hain jo publicly release nahi hote, sirf internally stronger models banane ke liye use hote hain. Open models me common practice hai closed API models se data distill karke chhote open weights me daalna. High-quality prompts curate karna aur teacher responses filter karna crucial hai.
Q28RLAIF kya hai — AI feedback human feedback ko replace kar sakta hai?
RLAIF — Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback — ek approach hai jahan AI human data wale pipeline ke hisse ko approximate karta hai. Cost ka farak huge hai: ek human preference data point ki cost lagbhag $1 ya zyada (kabhi $10+ per prompt), jabki frontier AI model se AI feedback $0.01 se kam ka hota hai. Early kaam dikhata hai ki AI feedback human data ko completely replace kar sakta hai, khaas taur par chat tasks par. Lekin nuanced picture ye hai: optimal equilibrium me challenging data-points humans ko route kiye jaate hain aur zyada tar data AI feedback se label hota hai. Rule of thumb: human data high-noise aur low-bias hai (reliable lekin mushkil), synthetic data low-noise aur high-bias hai (aasan lekin systematic second-order effects).
Q29Constitutional AI kya hai — do tareeke samjhao?
Constitutional AI (CAI) ek leading lab ke Claude models me use hone wala method hai — RLHF training ke liye synthetic data ka sabse pehla documented large-scale use. Do tareeke: (1) Instruction data ki critiques — model apne answers ko constitution (human-written principles ka set, jaise 'Is the answer encouraging violence?') ke against check karke refine karta hai, phir us dataset par fine-tune hota hai. (2) Pairwise preference data — language model decide karta hai kaunsi completion behtar hai, constitution se ek random principle ka context de kar — phir RLHF normal jaise proceed karta hai synthetic data ke saath, isi liye RLAIF naam. CAI woh example tha jisne RLAIF ke broader field ko kickstart kiya.
Q30Rubrics kya hain aur RLVR me kaise use hote hain?
Rubrics nearly-verifiable criteria hain un prompts ke liye jinke clearly verifiable answers nahi hain — jaise museum exhibit ke liye paanch artifacts suggest karna. Har rubric item ek testable criterion hota hai, [Hard Rule] ya [Principle] tag ke saath, aur weight ke saath (Essential/Important ke liye 1-5, Pitfall ke liye −1 ya −2). Model multiple answers generate karta hai aur RL se best answers ki taraf update hota hai — rubric scores ko reward banakar. Rubric generation per-prompt hoti hai (costly), to aksar per-domain general rubric starting point hoti hai aur supervising model per-prompt scores assign karta hai. Rubric-based RL scientific reasoning aur factuality me meaningful improvements deta hai.
Q31Tool use aur function calling kya hai — model tools kaise use karta hai?
Tool use ka matlab hai model ek structured request emit karta hai (tool name aur arguments), orchestrator tool execute karta hai, results context me append hote hain, aur model generate karna continue karta hai. Function calling tool use hai jahan arguments ko declared schema (usually JSON Schema) conform karna hota hai — reliable parsing aur validation ke liye. Code execution ek special case hai jahan tool ek code interpreter hai — jaise pi ko 50 digits tak compute karna bina hallucination ke. Model Context Protocol (MCP) ek open standard hai language models ko external data sources aur tools se connect karne ke liye, data layer par JSON-RPC use karke. Tool use training me SFT trajectories sikhata hai, DPO tool-call decisions improve karta hai, aur agentic tasks ke liye environment feedback wala RL natural objective hai.
Q32Chattiness kya hai — RLHF responses ko lamba kyun banata hai?
Chattiness ka matlab hai RLHF se train kiye gaye models se responses ki badhti hui length — plus heavy markdown, emojis aur bulleted lists. Reason: ChatBotArena jaise evaluations ne dikhaya hai ki average users longer, complete answers pasand karte hain jab unhe terse responses se compare kiya jaaye — longer answers zyada thorough, helpful ya trustworthy feel hote hain. Models bahut se data labelers ki average preferences match karne ke liye train hote hain, to RLHF verbosity badhata hai. Lekin ye tradeoff hai: DPO human preference evaluation improve karta hai lekin benchmark evaluation degrade kar sakta hai. AlpacaEval aur WildBench me linear length correction mechanisms hain taaki chattiness par doping ke incentives patch ho jaayein.
Q33KL penalty kyun lagate hain — reverse KL kya hai?
KL penalty RL policy ko reference policy ke kareeb rakhta hai: r = r_θ − λ_KL × D_KL(π_RL ∥ π_ref). Iske bina RL optimizer reward model ko over-optimize karke nonsensical text output karne lagta hai — repeated text, language switching, ya excessive special characters. Reverse KL (D_KL(P∥Q), P = naya model, Q = reference) bada penalty lagata hai jab naya model wahan probability mass rakhta hai jahan reference low probability deta hai. Implementation me KL ko Monte Carlo estimate se approximate karte hain: E[log P(x) − log Q(x)] — dono models ke log-probs se. Bahut bada KL divergence training me potential bug ya broken model indicate kar sakta hai.
Q34Over-optimization kya hai aur Goodhart ka law kya kehta hai?
Over-optimization tab hota hai jab training metric (proxy objective) final evaluations se mismatch ho jaata hai — model proxy par genuinely improve karta hai lekin true goal se door ho jaata hai. Example: reward model ka score chadhta rehta hai lekin downstream quality pehle badh kar phir girne lagti hai (Fig 16.1) — train reward model par improvements test reward model par lagbhag 150K samples ke baad transfer nahi karte. Ye overfitting se alag hai: overfitting me model training data memorize karta hai, over-optimization me metric hi galat tha. Goodhart ka law: 'When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.' Mitigations: KL penalty, reward model ensembles, bade policy models, aur DAA me fixed KL distances.
Q35External evaluation comparisons unreliable kyun hain — contamination kya hai?
AI companies ke model announcements ki evaluations ko sirf large error bars ke saath compare kiya jaa sakta hai — kyunki har lab ki internal process control nahi hoti ya document nahi hoti. Olmo 3 project me paaya gaya ki post-training evaluations me 0.25 se 1.5 point standard deviations hote hain jab setup constant rakha jaata hai — bade changes alag prompts ya sampling parameters se aate hain. Contamination ka matlab hai evaluation datasets ka data training me leak hona — jaise benchmarks public web par list hote hain aur crawl ho jaate hain. Tülu 3 ki decontamination me mila: UltraFeedback TruthfulQA se, Evol-CodeAlpaca HumanEval se, NuminaMath MATH se contaminate the — 8-gram overlap se detect hue. Isi liye apne models par apni evaluations chalana hi repeatable signal paane ka tareeka hai.
Q36Character training aur Model Spec kya hain?
Character training post-training ka woh subset hai jo model ki personality ya manner craft karta hai — content ki jagah. Prompting se zyada robust hai: fine-tuning se traits jaise curiosity, open-mindedness aur thoughtfulness instill kiye jaate hain — Constitutional AI jaisi pipeline se, lekin human data ke bina. Ye dikhata hai ki RLHF alignment ki philosophical motivations se shift karke ek empirical, product-facing tool ban gaya hai. Model Spec ek document hai jo fine-tuning run se pehle goal model behaviors detail karta hai — ye industry ke kuch tools me se ek hai jahan actual behavior ko designers ke intended behavior se compare kiya jaa sakta hai. Ye stakeholders — designers, developers aur public — sab ke liye valuable hai.
